speaker: Dhritarashtra
sanskrit:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya || 1 ||
translation: On the holy plain, on the field of Kuru, gathered together, eager for battle, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people and the Pândavas?

translator_notes.text: The common ancestor of the contending parties, the Kurus and the Pândavas, in the impending battle.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 1, p. 1

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ।
आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā |
ācāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vacanamabravīt || 2 ||
translation: Having seen arrayed the army of the Pândavas, the Prince Duryodhana approached his teacher, and spake these words:

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 2, p. 1–2

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् ।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā || 3 ||
translation: "Behold this mighty host of the sons of Pându, O teacher, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 3, p. 2

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि ।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi |
yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ || 4 ||
translation: Heroes are these, mighty bowmen, to Bhîma and Arjuna equal in battle: Yuyudhâna, Virâta, and Drupada of the great car.

translator_notes.text: One able to fight alone ten thousand bowmen.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 4, p. 2

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān |
purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ || 5 ||
translation: Drishtaketu, Chekitâna and the valiant King of Kâshi, Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, bull among men;

translator_notes.text: The bull, as the emblem of manly strength and vigour, is often used as an epithet of honour.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 5, p. 2–3

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān |
saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ || 6 ||
translation: Yudhâmanyu the strong, and Uttamaujas the brave; Saubhadra and the Draupadeyas, all of great cars.

translator_notes.text: Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadrâ and Arjuna.
The sons and grandsons of Drupada.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 6, p. 3

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama |
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te || 7 ||
translation: Know further all those who are our chiefs, O best of the twice-born, the leaders of my army; these I name to thee for thy information:

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 7, p. 3

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः ।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiñjayaḥ |
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca || 8 ||
translation: Thou, Lord, and Bhîshma, and Karna and Kripa, conquering in battle; Ashvatthâmâ, Vikarna, and Saumadatti also;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 8, p. 3–4

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ |
nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ || 9 ||
translation: And many others, heroes, for my sake renouncing their lives, with divers weapons and missiles, and all well-skilled in war.

corrections.basis: Flagged [sic] by Wikisource transcribers; printed reading kept (correct archaic usage).

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 9, p. 4

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
paryāptaṃ tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam || 10 ||
translation: Yet insufficient seems this army of ours, though marshalled by Bhîshma, while that army of theirs seems sufficient, though marshalled by Bhîma;

translator_notes.text: The commentators differ in their interpretation of this verse; Anandagiri takes it to mean just the reverse of Shridhara Svâmi, "aparyâptam" being taken by the one as "insufficient," by the other as "unlimited."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 10, p. 4

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ |
bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi || 11 ||
translation: Therefore in the rank and file let all, standing firmly in their respective divisions, guard Bhîshma, even all ye generals.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 11, p. 5

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
tasya sañjanayanharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān || 12 ||
translation: To enhearten him, the Ancient of the Kurus, the Grandsire, the glorious, blew his conch, sounding on high a lion's roar.

cross_checks.other_text:
तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 12, p. 5

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः ।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ |
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat || 13 ||
translation: Then conches and kettledrums, tabors and drums and cowhorns, suddenly blared forth, and the sound was tumultuous.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 13, p. 5

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau |
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ || 14 ||
translation: Then, stationed in their great war-chariot, yoked to white horses, Mâdhava and the son of Pându blew their divine conches.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 14, p. 6

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ || 15 ||
translation: Pânchajanya by Hrishîkesha, and Devadatta by Dhananjaya. Vrikodara of terrible deeds blew his mighty conch, Paundra;

translator_notes.text: Pânchajanya, Shri Krishna's conch, was made from the bones of the giant Panchajana, slain by him. The title Hrishîkesha is "Lord of the senses." Dhananjaya, the "conqueror of wealth," is a title often given to Arjuna, whose conch is the "God-given."
Bhîma; the meaning of the name of his conch is doubtful.

cross_checks.other_text:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 15, p. 6

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau || 16 ||
translation: The King Yudhishthira, the son of Kuntî, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

translator_notes.text: The conches of the remaining three brothers were named respectively "endless victory," "honey-tone," and "jewel-blossom."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 16, p. 6–7

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः ।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ |
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ || 17 ||
translation: And Kâshya, of the great bow and Shikhandî, the mighty car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna and Virâta and Sâtyaki, the unconquered.

translator_notes.text: The King of Kâshi, the modern Benares.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 17, p. 7

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते ।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate |
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak || 18 ||
translation: Drupada and the Draupadeyas, O Lord of earth, and Saubhadra, the mighty-armed, on all sides their several conches blew.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 18, p. 7

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan || 19 ||
translation: That tumultuous uproar rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarâshtra, filling the earth and sky with sound.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 19, p. 7–8

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः ।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrānkapidhvajaḥ |
pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ || 20 ||
translation: Then, beholding the sons of Dhritarâshtra standing arrayed, and flight of missiles about to begin, he whose crest is an ape, the son of Pându, took up his bow,

cross_checks.other_text:
अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 20, p. 8

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate |
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta || 21 ||
translation: And spake this word to Hrishîkesha, O Lord of Earth: Arjuna said: In the midst, between the two armies, stay my chariot, O Achyuta,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 21, p. 8

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्‌धुकामानवस्थितान् ।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
yāvadetānnirīkṣe'haṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān |
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasminraṇasamudyame || 22 ||
translation: That I may behold these standing, longing for battle, with whom I must strive in this outbreaking war,

cross_checks.other_text:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 22, p. 9

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṃ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ || 23 ||
translation: And gaze on those here gathered together ready to fight, desirous of pleasing in battle the evil-minded son of Dhritarâshtra.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 23, p. 9

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam || 24 ||
translation: Thus addressed by Gudâkesha, Hrishîkesha, O Bhârata, having stayed that best of chariots in the midst, between the two armies,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 24, p. 9

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् ।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti || 25 ||
translation: Over against Bhîshma, Drona and all the rulers of the world, said: "O Pârtha, behold these Kurus gathered together."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 25, p. 10

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान् ।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān |
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṝnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā || 26 ||
translation: Then saw Pârtha standing there, uncles and grandfathers, teachers, mother's brothers, cousins, sons and grandsons, comrades,

cross_checks.other_text:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान्।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 26, p. 10

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi |
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān || 27 ||
translation: Fathers-in-law and benefactors also in both armies; seeing all these kinsmen thus standing arrayed, Kaunteya,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 1, verse 27, p. 10

speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:

हत्वाऽर्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान्रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ ५ ॥

translation: Better in this world to eat even the beggar's crust than to slay these most noble Gurus. Slaying these Gurus, our well-wishers, I should taste of blood-besprinkled feasts.

translator_notes.text: More often translated, "desirous of wealth," but the word is used elsewhere for well-wisher, "desirous of good," and the term is more in accordance with the tone of Arjuna's remarks.

sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam || 32 ||

sanskrit:

bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām || 41 ||

transliteration:

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:

क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ ४३ ॥

kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati || 43 ||
translation: With desire for self, with heaven for goal, they offer birth as the fruit of action, and prescribe many and various ceremonies for the attainment of pleasure and lordship.

translator_notes.text: Those whose very self is desire, Kâma, and who therefore act with a view to win heaven and also rebirth to wealth and rank.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 43, p. 33

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयाऽपहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
transliteration:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayā'pahṛtacetasām |
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate || 44 ||
translation: For them who cling to pleasure and lordship, whose minds are captivated by such teaching, is not designed this determinate Reason, on contemplation steadily bent.

translator_notes.text: Samadhi, the third state of consciousness in meditation.

The following alternative translation of Slokas 42, 43, and 44 is offered: "The flowery speech that the unwise utter, O Pârtha, clinging to the word of the Veda, saying there is nothing else, ensouled by desire and longing after heaven, (the speech) that offereth only rebirth as the (ultimate) fruit of action, that is full of (recommendations to) various rites for the sake of (gaining) enjoyments and sovereignty—the thought of those misled by that (speech), cleaving to pleasures and lordship, not being inspired with resolution, is not engaged in contemplation." This is closer to the original, which is all in one sentence.

sanskrit:

translation: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes, O Arjuna; beyond the pairs of opposites, ever steadfast in purity, careless of possessions, full of the Self.

translator_notes.text: Gunas = attributes, or forms of energy. They are sattva, rhythm, harmony, or purity; rajas, motion, activity, or passion; tamas, inertia, darkness, or stupidity.

speaker: Krishna

translation: All the Vedas are as useful to an enlightened Brâhmana as is a tank in a place covered all over with water.

sanskrit:

sanskrit:

translation: Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine, renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga.

translation: Far lower than the Yoga of Discrimination is action, O Dhananjaya. Take thou refuge in the Pure Reason; pitiable are they who work for fruit.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:

तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
transliteration:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam || 50 ||
translation: United to the Pure Reason one abandoneth here both good and evil deeds; therefore cleave thou to yoga; yoga is skill in action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 50, p. 36

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
transliteration:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam || 51 ||
translation: The Sages, united to the Pure Reason, renounce the fruit which action yieldeth, and, liberated from the bonds of birth, they go to the blissful seat.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 51, p. 36–37

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ ५२ ॥
transliteration:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati |
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca || 52 ||
translation: When thy mind shall escape from this tangle of delusion, then thou shalt rise to indifference as to what has been heard and shall be heard.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 52, p. 37

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
transliteration:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi || 53 ||
translation: When thy mind, bewildered by the Scriptures, shall stand immovable, fixed in contemplation, then shalt thou attain unto yoga.

translator_notes.text: To union with Atma, the Self ; yoga implies harmony with the divine will. The word translated contemplation is, as before, Samâdhi.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 53, p. 37

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
transliteration:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim || 54 ||
translation: What the mark, of him who is stable of mind, steadfast in contemplation, O Keshava? How doth the stable-minded talk, how doth he sit, how walk?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 54, p. 37–38

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
transliteration:
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān |
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate || 55 ||
translation: When a man abandoneth, O Pârtha, all the desires of the heart, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he called stable in mind.

cross_checks.other_text:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 55, p. 38

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
transliteration:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ |
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate || 56 ||
translation: He whose mind is free from anxiety amid pains, indifferent amid pleasures, loosed from passion, fear and anger, is called a sage of stable mind.

translator_notes.text: A Muni, i.e. , a saint or ascetic: in its original meaning, one who observed the vow of silence.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 56, p. 38–39

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
transliteration:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham |
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 57 ||
translation: He who on every side is without attachments, whatever hap of fair and foul, who neither likes nor dislikes, of such a one the understanding is well poised.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 57, p. 39

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
transliteration:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 58 ||
translation: When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding well poised.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 58, p. 39

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
transliteration:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate || 59 ||
translation: The objects of sense, but not the relish for them, turn away from an abstemious dweller in the body; and even relish turneth away from him after the Supreme is seen.

translator_notes.text: The objects turn away when rejected, but still desire for them remains; even desire is lost when the Supreme is seen.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 59, p. 39–40

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ ६० ॥
transliteration:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ || 60 ||
translation: O son of Kuntî, the excited senses of even a wise man, though he be striving, impetuously carry away his mind.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 60, p. 40

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
transliteration:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ |
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 61 ||
translation: Having restrained them all, he should sit harmonised, I his supreme goal; for, whose senses are mastered, of him the understanding is well poised.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 61, p. 40

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate |
saṅgātsañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate || 62 ||
translation: Man, musing on the objects of sense, conceiveth an attachment to these; from attachment ariseth desire; from desire anger cometh forth;

cross_checks.other_text:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 62, p. 41

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
transliteration:
krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ |
smṛtibhraṃśādbuddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati || 63 ||
translation: From anger proceedeth delusion; from delusion confused memory; from confused memory the destruction of Reason; from destruction of Reason he perishes.

cross_checks.other_text:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 63, p. 41

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
transliteration:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran |
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati || 64 ||
translation: But the disciplined self, moving among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and repulsion, mastered by the Self, goeth to peace.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 64, p. 41

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
transliteration:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate |
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate || 65 ||
translation: In that Peace the extinction of all pains ariseth for him, for of him whose heart is peaceful the Reason soon attaineth equilibrium.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 65, p. 42

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
transliteration:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham || 66 ||
translation: There is no Pure Reason for the non-harmonised, nor for the non-harmonised is there concentration; for him without concentration there is no peace, and for the unpeaceful how can there be happiness?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 66, p. 42

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ ६७ ॥
transliteration:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nu vidhīyate |
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi || 67 ||
translation: Such of the roving senses as the mind yieldeth to, that hurries away the understanding, just as the gale hurries away a ship upon the waters.

cross_checks.other_text:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 67, p. 42–43

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
transliteration:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 68 ||
translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed, whose senses are all completely restrained from the objects of sense, of him the understanding is well poised.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 68, p. 43

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
transliteration:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ || 69 ||
translation: That which is the night of all beings, for the disciplined man is the time of waking; when other beings are waking, then is it night for the sage who seeth.

translator_notes.text: The sage is awake to things over which the ordinary man sleeps and the eyes of the sage are open to truths shut out from the common vision, while vice versa that which is real for the masses is illusion for the sage.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 69, p. 43

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
transliteration:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī || 70 ||
translation: He attaineth Peace, into whom all desires flow as rivers flow into the ocean, which is filled with water, but remaineth unmoved—not he who desireth desires.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 70, p. 43–44

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
transliteration:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati || 71 ||
translation: Whoso forsaketh all desires and goeth onwards free from yearnings, selfless and without egoism—he goeth to Peace.

cross_checks.other_text:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 71, p. 44

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्म निर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
transliteration:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitvā'syāmantakāle'pi brahma nirvāṇamṛcchati || 72 ||
translation: This is the Eternal state, O son of Prithâ. Having attained thereto, none is bewildered. Who, even at the death-hour, is established therein, he goeth to the Nirvâna of the Eternal.

cross_checks.other_text:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 2, verse 72, p. 44

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana |
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava || 1 ||
translation: If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janârdana, why dost Thou, O Keshava, enjoin on me this terrible action?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 1, p. 46

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me |
tadekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām || 2 ||
translation: With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss.

cross_checks.other_text:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।
तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 2, p. 46

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयाऽनघ ।
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayā'nagha |
jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām || 3 ||
translation: In this world there is a twofold path, as I before said, O sinless one: that of yoga by knowledge, of the Sâñkhyas; and that of yoga by action, of the Yogis.

cross_checks.other_text:
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।
ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 3, p. 46–47

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते ।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo'śnute |
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati || 4 ||
translation: Man winneth not freedom from action by abstaining from activity, nor by mere renunciation doth he rise to perfection.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 4, p. 47

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् ।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt |
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ || 5 ||
translation: Nor can anyone, even for an instant, remain really actionless; for helplessly is everyone driven to action by the qualities born of nature.

cross_checks.other_text:
न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 5, p. 47

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate || 6 ||
translation: Who sitteth, controlling the organs of action, but dwelling in his mind on the objects of the senses, that bewildered man is called a hypocrite.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 6, p. 47–48

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन ।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna |
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate || 7 ||
translation: But who, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, with the organs of action without attachment, performeth yoga by action, he is worthy.

translator_notes.text: Karma-Yoga is the consecration of physical energy on the divine Altar; i.e. , the using of one's organs of action simply in service, in obedience to Law and Duty.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 7, p. 48

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
शरीरयात्राऽपि च ते न प्रसिध्येदकर्मणः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ |
śarīrayātrā'pi ca te na prasidhyedakarmaṇaḥ || 8 ||
translation: Perform thou right action, for, action is superior to inaction, and, inactive, even the maintenance of thy body would not be possible.

translator_notes.text: Regulated, prescribed as a duty; or, regularly.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Not applied: the printed reading agrees with the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 8, p. 48

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara || 9 ||
translation: The world is bound by action, unless performed for the sake of sacrifice; for that sake, free from attachment, O son of Kuntî, perform thou action.

cross_checks.other_text:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 9, p. 49

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk || 10 ||
translation: Having in ancient times emanated mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of emanation said: "By this shall ye propagate; be this to you the giver of desire;

translator_notes.text: Kâmadhuk, the cow of Indra, from which each could milk what he wished for; hence the giver of desired objects.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 10, p. 49

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha || 11 ||
translation: "With this nourish ye the Shining Ones, and may the Shining Ones nourish you; thus nourishing one another ye shall reap the supremest good.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 11, p. 49–50

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ |
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ || 12 ||
translation: "For, nourished by sacrifice, the Shining Ones shall bestow on you the enjoyments you desire." A thief verily is he who enjoyeth what is given by Them without returning Them aught.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 12, p. 50

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ |
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt || 13 ||
translation: The righteous, who eat the remains of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the impious, who dress food for their own sakes, they verily eat sin.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 13, p. 50

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसंभवः ।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasaṃbhavaḥ |
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ || 14 ||
translation: From food creatures become; from rain is the production of food; rain proceedeth from sacrifice; sacrifice ariseth out of action.

cross_checks.other_text:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 14, p. 50–51

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माऽक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmā'kṣarasamudbhavam |
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam || 15 ||
translation: Know thou that from Brahma action groweth, and Brahma from the Imperishable cometh. Therefore the Eternal, the all-permeating, is ever present in sacrifice.

translator_notes.text: An Indian of much knowledge translates Brahma here as "the Vedas."

cross_checks.other_text:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 15, p. 51

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati || 16 ||
translation: He who on earth doth not follow the wheel thus revolving, sinful of life and rejoicing in the senses, he, O son of Pritha, liveth in vain.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 16, p. 51

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः ।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ |
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate || 17 ||
translation: But the man who rejoiceth in the Self, with the Self is satisfied, and is content in the Self, for him verily there is nothing to do;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 17, p. 51–52

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ || 18 ||
translation: For him there is no interest in things done, in this world, nor any in things not done, nor doth any object of his depend on any being.

cross_checks.other_text:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 18, p. 52

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ || 19 ||
translation: Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform action which is duty, for, by performing action without attachment, man verily reacheth the Supreme.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 19, p. 52

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।
लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ |
lokasaṅgrahamevāpi sampaśyankartumarhasi || 20 ||
translation: Janaka and others indeed attained to perfection by action: then having an eye to the welfare of the world also, thou shouldst perform action.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

cross_checks.other_text:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 20, p. 52

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ |
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate || 21 ||
translation: Whatsoever a great man doeth, that other men also do; the standard he setteth up, by that the people go.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 21, p. 53

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana |
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi || 22 ||
translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Pârtha, that should be done by Me, nor anything unattained that might be attained; yet I mingle in action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 22, p. 53

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ || 23 ||
translation: For if I mingled not ever in action unwearied, men all around would follow My path, O son of Prithâ.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 23, p. 53

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham |
saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ || 24 ||
translation: These worlds would fall into ruin, if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 24, p. 53–54

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत ।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथाऽसक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसङ्ग्रहम् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
kuryādvidvāṃstathā'saktaścikīrṣurlokasaṅgraham || 25 ||
translation: As the ignorant act from attachment to action, O Bhârata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.

cross_checks.other_text:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 25, p. 54

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām |
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran || 26 ||
translation: Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people attached to action; but acting in harmony with Me let him render all action attractive.

cross_checks.other_text:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 26, p. 54

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः ।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartā'hamiti manyate || 27 ||
translation: All actions are wrought by the qualities of nature only. The self, deluded by egoism, thinketh: "I am the doer."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 27, p. 54–55

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः ।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ |
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate || 28 ||
translation: But he, O mighty-armed, who knoweth the essence of the divisions of the qualities and functions, holding that "the qualities move amid the qualities," is not attached.

translator_notes.text: The Gunas, qualities, as sense-organs move amid the Gunas, qualities, as sense-objects. A suggested reading is "The functions dwell in the propensities." Sankarâchârya says, "of the class of qualities and the class of actions;" or the arrangement, or relations of qualities and actions.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 28, p. 55

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु ।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu |
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet || 29 ||
translation: Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish whose knowledge is imperfect.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 29, p. 55

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याऽध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyā'dhyātmacetasā |
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ || 30 ||
translation: Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy thoughts resting on the supreme Self, from hope and egoism freed, and of mental fever cured, engage in battle.

cross_checks.other_text:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 30, p. 56

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante te'pi karmabhiḥ || 31 ||
translation: Who abide ever in this teaching of Mine full of faith and free from caviling, they too are released from actions.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 31, p. 56

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ || 32 ||
translation: Who carp at My teaching and act not thereon, senseless, deluded in all knowledge, know thou these mindless ones as fated to be destroyed.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 32, p. 56

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि ।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi |
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati || 33 ||
translation: Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings follow nature; what shall restraint avail?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 33, p. 56–57

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau |
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau || 34 ||
translation: Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 34, p. 57

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ || 35 ||
translation: Better one's own duty, though destitute of merit, than the duty of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is full of danger.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 35, p. 57

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ || 36 ||
translation: But dragged on by what does a man commit sin, reluctantly indeed, O Varshneya, as it were by force constrained?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 36, p. 57–58

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ |
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam || 37 ||
translation: It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 37, p. 58

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
धूमेनाऽव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च ।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
dhūmenā'vriyate vahniryathā''darśo malena ca |
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam || 38 ||
translation: As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This is enveloped by it.

translator_notes.text: The universe: " This " as opposed to " That " the Eternal . Some say " This " stands for knowledge.

cross_checks.other_text:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 38, p. 58

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā |
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca || 39 ||
translation: Enveloped is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is insatiable as a flame.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 39, p. 58–59

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate |
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam || 40 ||
translation: The senses, the mind and the Reason are said to be its seat; by these enveloping wisdom, it bewilders the dweller in the body.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 40, p. 59

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha |
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam || 41 ||
translation: Therefore, O best of the Bhâratas, mastering first the senses, do thou slay this thing of sin, destructive of wisdom and knowledge.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 41, p. 59

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ || 42 ||
translation: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 42, p. 59

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥ ४३ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā |
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam || 43 ||
translation: Thus understanding Him as greater than the Reason, restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, difficult to overcome.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 3, verse 43, p. 60

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् ।
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam |
vivasvānmanave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt || 1 ||
translation: This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvân; Vivasvân taught it to Manu; Manu to Ikshvâku told it.

cross_checks.other_text:
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।
विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 1, p. 61

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ |
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa || 2 ||
translation: This, handed on down the line, the King-Sages knew. This yoga by great efflux of time decayed in the world, O Parantapa.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 2, p. 61

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
स एवाऽयं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
sa evā'yaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ |
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam || 3 ||
translation: This same ancient yoga hath been to-day declared to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme Secret.

cross_checks.other_text:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 3, p. 61

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti || 4 ||
translation: Later was Thy birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvân; how then am I to understand that Thou declaredst it in the beginning?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 4, p. 62

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन ।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna |
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa || 5 ||
translation: Many births have been left behind by Me and by thee, O Arjuna. I know them all, but thou knowest not thine, O Parantapa.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 5, p. 62

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् ।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san |
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmyātmamāyayā || 6 ||
translation: Though unborn, the imperishable Self, and also the Lord of all beings, brooding over nature which is Mine own, yet I am born through My own Power.

translator_notes.text: Mâyâ, the power of thought that produces form, which is transient and therefore unreal compared with the eternal Reality; hence Mâyâ comes to be taken as the power of producing illusion.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 6, p. 62–63

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadā''tmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham || 7 ||
translation: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

translator_notes.text: Adharma, the opposite of dharma, all that is disorderly, against the nature of things.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 7, p. 63

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge || 8 ||
translation: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

cross_checks.other_text:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 8, p. 63

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna || 9 ||
translation: He who thus knoweth My divine birth and action, in its essence, having abandoned the body, cometh not to birth again, but cometh unto Me, O Arjuna.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 9, p. 63–64

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ |
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ || 10 ||
translation: Freed from passion, fear and anger, filled with Me, taking refuge in Me, purified in the fire of wisdom, many have entered into My Being.

translator_notes.text: Tapas, from tap, blazing like fire.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 10, p. 64

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ || 11 ||
translation: However men approach Me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side is Mine, O Pârtha.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 11, p. 64

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā || 12 ||
translation: They who long after success in action on earth worship the Shining Ones; for in brief space verily, in this world of men, success is born of action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 12, p. 65

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam || 13 ||
translation: The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 13, p. 65

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बद्ध्यते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā |
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa baddhyate || 14 ||
translation: Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions.

cross_checks.other_text:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 14, p. 65

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ |
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam || 15 ||
translation: Having thus known, our forefathers, ever seeking liberation, performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did our forefathers in the olden time.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 15, p. 66

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ |
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt || 16 ||
translation: "What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 16, p. 66

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ || 17 ||
translation: It is needful to discriminate action, to discriminate unlawful action, and to discriminate inaction; mysterious is the path of action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 17, p. 66

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt || 18 ||
translation: He who seeth inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is harmonious, even while performing all action.

cross_checks.other_text:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 18, p. 67

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ |
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ || 19 ||
translation: Whose works are all free from the moulding of desire, whose actions are burned up by the fire of wisdom, him the wise have called a Sage.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 19, p. 67

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ || 20 ||
translation: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, always content, nowhere seeking refuge, he is not doing anything, although doing actions.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 20, p. 67

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 21 ||
translation: Hoping for naught, his mind and self controlled, having abandoned all greed, performing action by the body alone, he doth not commit sin.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 21, p. 67–68

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वाऽपि न निबध्यते ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvā'pi na nibadhyate || 22 ||
translation: Content with whatsoever he obtaineth without effort, free from the pairs of opposites, without envy, balanced in success and failure, though acting he is not bound.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Not applied: the printed reading agrees with the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 22, p. 68

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate || 23 ||
translation: Of one with attachment dead, harmonious, with his thoughts established in wisdom, his works sacrifices, all action melts away.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 23, p. 68

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā || 24 ||
translation: The Eternal the oblation, the Eternal the clarified butter, are offered in the Eternal the fire by the Eternal; unto the Eternal verily shall he go who in his action meditateth wholly upon the Eternal.

translator_notes.text: He who sees the Eternal beneath the transitory alone goes to the Eternal ; all others remain bound in the world of forms.

cross_checks.other_text:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 24, p. 68–69

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते ।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati || 25 ||
translation: Some Yogis offer up sacrifice to the Shining Ones; others sacrifice only by pouring sacrifice into the fire of the Eternal;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 25, p. 69

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati |
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati || 26 ||
translation: Some pour as sacrifice hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint; some pour sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses as sacrifice;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 26, p. 69

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare |
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite || 27 ||
translation: Others again into the wisdom-kindled fire of union attained by self-control, pour as sacrifice all the functions of the senses and the functions of life;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 27, p. 70

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथाऽपरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathā'pare |
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ || 28 ||
translation: Yet others the sacrifice of wealth, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of yoga, the sacrifice of silent reading and wisdom, men concentrated and of effectual vows;

cross_checks.other_text:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 28, p. 70

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे ।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe'pānaṃ tathā'pare |
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ || 29 ||
translation: Yet others pour as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the control of breathing.

translator_notes.text: Prânâyâma, restraint of breath, a technical name for this practice.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 29, p. 70–71

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati |
sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ || 30 ||
translation: Others regular in food, pour as sacrifice their life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, and by sacrifice have destroyed their sins.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 30, p. 71

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |
nāyaṃ loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama || 31 ||
translation: The eaters of the life-giving remains of sacrifice go to the changeless Eternal. This world is not for the non-sacrificer, much less the other, O best of the Kurus.

translator_notes.text: Amrita: it is the elixir of immortality, and the amrita-remains, therefore, are foods that give immortality.

cross_checks.other_text:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 31, p. 71

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase || 32 ||
translation: Many and various sacrifices are thus spread out before the Eternal. Know thou that all these are born of action, and thus knowing thou shalt be free.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 32, p. 72

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप ।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa |
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate || 33 ||
translation: Better than the sacrifice of any objects is the sacrifice of wisdom, O Parantapa. All actions in their entirety, O Pârtha, culminate in wisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 33, p. 72

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ || 34 ||
translation: Learn thou this by discipleship, by investigation, and by service. The wise, the seers of the essence of things, will instruct thee in wisdom.

translator_notes.text: Literally, falling at the feet, i.e. , the feet of the teacher.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 34, p. 72–73

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
yena bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi || 35 ||
translation: And having known this, thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pândava; for by this thou wilt see all beings without exception in the Self, and thus in Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 35, p. 73

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः ।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ |
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi || 36 ||
translation: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet shalt thou cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 36, p. 73

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā || 37 ||
translation: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 37, p. 73

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate |
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati || 38 ||
translation: Verily there is no purifier in this world like wisdom; he that is perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in due season.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 38, p. 74

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati || 39 ||
translation: The man who is full of faith obtaineth wisdom, and he also who hath mastery over his senses; and, having obtained wisdom, he goeth swiftly to the supreme Peace.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 39, p. 74

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ || 40 ||
translation: But the ignorant, faithless, doubting self goeth to destruction; nor this world, nor that beyond, nor happiness, is there for the doubting self.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 40, p. 74

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam |
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya || 41 ||
translation: He who hath renounced actions by yoga, who hath cloven asunder doubt by wisdom, who is ruled by the Self, actions do not bind him, O Dhananjaya.

cross_checks.other_text:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम्।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 41, p. 75

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
tasmādajñānasambhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinā''tmanaḥ |
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata || 42 ||
translation: Therefore, with the sword of the wisdom of the Self cleaving asunder this ignorance-born doubt dwelling in thy heart, be established in yoga. Stand up, O Bhârata.

cross_checks.other_text:
तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 4, verse 42, p. 75

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि ।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
yacchreya etayorekaṃ tanme brūhi suniścitam || 1 ||
translation: Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively.

cross_checks.other_text:
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 1, p. 76

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau |
tayostu karmasaṃnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate || 2 ||
translation: Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 2, p. 76

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
