nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhātpramucyate || 3 ||
translation: He should be known as a perpetual ascetic, who neither hateth nor desireth; free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 3, p. 76–77

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः ।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
sāṅkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam || 4 ||
translation: Children, not sages, speak of the Sânkhya and the Yoga as different; he who is duly established in one obtaineth the fruits of both.

cross_checks.other_text:
सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 4, p. 77

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate |
ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati || 5 ||
translation: That place which is gained by the Sânkhyas is reached by the Yogîs also. He seeth, who seeth that the Sânkhya and the Yoga are one.

cross_checks.other_text:
यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।
एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 5, p. 77

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
saṃnyāsastu mahābāho duḥkhamāptumayogataḥ |
yogayukto munirbrahma na cireṇādhigacchati || 6 ||
translation: But without yoga, O mighty-armed, renunciation is hard to attain to; the yoga-harmonised Muni swiftly goeth to the Eternal.

cross_checks.other_text:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः।
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 6, p. 77–78

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ |
sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate || 7 ||
translation: He who is harmonised by yoga, the self purified, Self-ruled, the senses subdued, whose Self is the Self of all beings, although acting he is not affected.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 7, p. 78

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ।
पश्यन्शृण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन्श्वसन् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
naiva kiñcitkaromīti yukto manyeta tattvavit |
paśyanśṛṇvanspṛśañjighrannaśnangacchansvapanśvasan || 8 ||
translation: "I do not anything," should think the harmonised one, who knoweth the essence of things; seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Not confirmed by the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text:
नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्।
पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 8, p. 78

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
pralapanvisṛjangṛhṇannunmiṣannimiṣannapi |
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan || 9 ||
translation: Speaking, giving, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, he holdeth: "The senses move among the objects of the senses."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 9, p. 78–79

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā || 10 ||
translation: He who acteth, placing all actions in the Eternal, abandoning attachment, is unaffected by sin as a lotus leaf by the waters.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 10, p. 79

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi |
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā''tmaśuddhaye || 11 ||
translation: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform action only by the body, by the mind, by the Reason, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self.

corrections.basis: Flagged [sic] by Wikisource transcribers; printed reading kept (no correction suggested).

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 11, p. 79

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate || 12 ||
translation: The harmonised man, having abandoned the fruit of action, attaineth to the eternal Peace; the non-harmonised, impelled by desire, attached to fruit, are bound.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 12, p. 79–80

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी ।
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī |
navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan || 13 ||
translation: Mentally renouncing all actions, the sovereign dweller in the body resteth serenely in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act.

translator_notes.text: The body, often called the city of the Eternal .

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 13, p. 80

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः ।
न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ |
na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate || 14 ||
translation: The Lord of the world produceth not the idea of agency, nor actions, nor the union together of action and its fruit; nature, however, manifesteth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 14, p. 80

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
nādatte kasyacitpāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ |
ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ || 15 ||
translation: The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 15, p. 80–81

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः ।
तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
jñānena tu tadajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitamātmanaḥ |
teṣāmādityavajjñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam || 16 ||
translation: Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the Self, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 16, p. 81

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।
गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ |
gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ || 17 ||
translation: Thinking on That, merged in That, established in That, solely devoted to That, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by wisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 17, p. 81

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
vidyāvinayasampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ || 18 ||
translation: Sages look equally on a Brâhmana adorned with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.

translator_notes.text: Shvapâka, the lowest class of outcastes.

cross_checks.other_text:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 18, p. 81–82

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ |
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ || 19 ||
translation: Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind remains balanced; the Eternal is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 19, p. 82

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् ।
स्थिरबुद्धिरसंमूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
na prahṛṣyetpriyaṃ prāpya nodvijetprāpya cāpriyam |
sthirabuddhirasaṃmūḍho brahmavidbrahmaṇi sthitaḥ || 20 ||
translation: With Reason firm, unperplexed, the knower of the Eternal established in the Eternal, neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant, nor sorroweth on obtaining what is unpleasant.

cross_checks.other_text:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्।
स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 20, p. 82

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् ।
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yatsukham |
sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukhamakṣayamaśnute || 21 ||
translation: He, whose self is unattached to external contacts and findeth joy in the Self, having the self harmonised with the Eternal by yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 21, p. 82–83

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te |
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ || 22 ||
translation: The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 22, p. 83

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक् शरीरविमोक्षणात् ।
कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīravimokṣaṇāt |
kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ || 23 ||
translation: He who is able to endure here on earth, ere he be liberated from the body, the force born from desire and passion, he is harmonised, he is a happy man.

cross_checks.other_text:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्।
कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 23, p. 83

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः ।
स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
yo'ntaḥsukho'ntarārāmastathāntarjyotireva yaḥ |
sa yogī brahmanirvāṇaṃ brahmabhūto'dhigacchati || 24 ||
translation: He who is happy within, who rejoiceth within, who is illuminated within, that Yogî, becoming the Eternal, goeth to the Peace of the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 24, p. 83–84

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।
छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ |
chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ || 25 ||
translation: Rishis, their sins destroyed, their duality removed, their selves controlled, intent upon the welfare of all beings, obtain the Peace of the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 25, p. 84

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् ।
अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām |
abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām || 26 ||
translation: The Peace of the Eternal lies near to those who know themselves, who are disjoined from desire and passion, subdued in nature, of subdued thoughts.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 26, p. 84

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः ।
प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṃścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ |
prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau || 27 ||
translation: Having external contacts excluded, and with gaze fixed between the eyebrows; having made equal the outgoing and ingoing breaths moving within the nostrils;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 27, p. 85

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः ।
विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ |
vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ || 28 ||
translation: With senses, mind, and Reason ever controlled, solely pursuing liberation, the Sage, having for ever cast away desire, fear and passion, verily is liberated.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 28, p. 85

division_title: The Yoga of the Renunciation of Action
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ।
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram |
suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati || 29 ||
translation: Having known Me, as the Enjoyer of sacrifice and of austerity, the mighty Ruler of all the worlds, and the Lover of all beings, he goeth to Peace.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 5, verse 29, p. 85–86

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ |
sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ || 1 ||
translation: He that performeth such action as his duty, independently of the fruit of action, he is an ascetic, he is a Yogî, not he that is without fire, and without rites.

translator_notes.text: The ascetic, the Sannyâsî, lights no sacrificial fire and performs no sacrifices nor ceremonies; but merely to omit these, without true renunciation, is not to be a real ascetic.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 1, p. 87

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
na hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana || 2 ||
translation: That which is called renunciation, know thou that as yoga, O Pândava; nor doth any one become a Yogî with the formative will unrenounced.

translator_notes.text: Sankalpa, the imaginative faculty that makes plans for the future.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 2, p. 87

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते ।
योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate |
yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate || 3 ||
translation: For a Sage who is seeking Yoga, action is called the means; for the same Sage, when he is enthroned in yoga, serenity is called the means.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 3, p. 88

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते ।
सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate |
sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate || 4 ||
translation: When a man feeleth no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, renouncing the formative will, then, he is said to be enthroned in yoga.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 4, p. 88

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
uddharedātmanā''tmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet |
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ || 5 ||
translation: Let him raise the self by the Self and not let the self become depressed; for verily is the Self the friend of the self, and also the Self the self's enemy;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 5, p. 88

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
bandhurātmā''tmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ |
anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat || 6 ||
translation: The Self is the friend of the self of him in whom the self by the Self is vanquished; but to the unsubdued self the Self verily becometh hostile as an enemy.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 6, p. 89

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ |
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ || 7 ||
translation: The higher Self of him who is Self-controlled and peaceful is uniform in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 7, p. 89

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ।
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ |
yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ || 8 ||
translation: The Yogî who is satisfied with wisdom and knowledge, unwavering, whose senses are subdued, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonised.

translator_notes.text: The word Yogi is used for any one who is practising yoga, as well as for the man who has attained union.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 8, p. 89–90

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु ।
साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu |
sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate || 9 ||
translation: He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 9, p. 90

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ || 10 ||
translation: Let the Yogî constantly engage himself in yoga, remaining in a secret place by himself, with thought and self subdued, free from hope and greed.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 10, p. 90

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः ।
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ |
nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram || 11 ||
translation: In a pure place, established on a fixed seat of his own, neither very much raised nor very low, made of a cloth, a black antelope skin, and kusha grass, one over the other;

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 11, p. 90–91

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः ।
उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ |
upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye || 12 ||
translation: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with thought and the functions of the senses subdued, steady on his seat, he should practise yoga for the purification of the self.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 12, p. 91

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः ।
संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ |
saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan || 13 ||
translation: Holding the body, head and neck erect, immovably steady, looking fixedly at the point of the nose, with unseeing gaze,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 13, p. 91

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः ।
मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ |
manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ || 14 ||
translation: The self serene, fearless, firm in the vow of the Brahmachâri, the mind controlled, thinking on Me, harmonised, let him sit aspiring after Me.

translator_notes.text: A Brahmachârî is a man who is keeping the vow of continence, a celibate.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 14, p. 91–92

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।
शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
yuñjannevaṃ sadā''tmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ |
śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati || 15 ||
translation: The Yogî ever united thus with the Self, with the mind controlled, goeth to Peace, to the supreme Bliss that abideth in Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 15, p. 92

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।
न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ |
na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna || 16 ||
translation: Verily yoga is not for him who eateth too much, nor who abstaineth to excess, nor who is too much addicted to sleep, nor even to wakefulness, O Arjuna.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 16, p. 92

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu |
yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā || 17 ||
translation: Yoga killeth out all pain for him who is regulated in eating and amusement, regulated in performing actions, regulated in sleeping and waking.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 17, p. 92–93

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते ।
निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate |
niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā || 18 ||
translation: When his subdued thought is fixed on the Self, free from longing after all desirable things, then it is said, "he is harmonised."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 18, p. 93

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ || 19 ||
translation: As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogî of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the Self.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 19, p. 93

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया ।
यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā |
yatra caivātmanā''tmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati || 20 ||
translation: That in which the mind finds rest, quieted by the practice of yoga: that in which he, seeing the Self by the Self, in the Self is satisfied;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 20, p. 93

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवाऽयं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
sukhamātyantikaṃ yattad buddhigrāhyamatīndriyam |
vetti yatra na caivā'yaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ || 21 ||
translation: That in which he findeth the supreme delight which the Reason can grasp beyond the senses, wherein established he moveth not from the Reality;

cross_checks.other_text:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 21, p. 94

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणाऽपि विचाल्यते ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ |
yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇā'pi vicālyate || 22 ||
translation: Which, having obtained, he thinketh there is no greater gain beyond it; wherein, established, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow;

cross_checks.other_text:
यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः।
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 22, p. 94

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तं विद्याद्‌ दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् ।
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam |
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā || 23 ||
translation: That should be known by the name of yoga, this disconnection from the union with pain. This yoga must be clung to with a firm conviction and with undesponding mind.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

cross_checks.other_text:

स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 23, p. 94

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सङ्कल्पप्रभावान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः ।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
saṅkalpaprabhāvānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ |
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ || 24 ||
translation: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of the imagination, by the mind curbing in the aggregate of the senses on every side,

cross_checks.other_text:
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 24, p. 95

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शनैःशनैरुपरमेद्‌ बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया ।
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
śanaiḥśanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā |
ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet || 25 ||
translation: Little by little let him gain tranquillity, by means of Reason controlled by steadiness; having made the mind abide in the Self, let him not think of anything.

cross_checks.other_text:
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया।
आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 25, p. 95

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram |
tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet || 26 ||
translation: As often as the wavering and unsteady mind goeth forth, so often reining it in, let him bring it under the control of the Self.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 26, p. 95

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् ।
उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
praśāntamanasaṃ hyenaṃ yoginaṃ sukhamuttamam |
upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam || 27 ||
translation: Supreme joy is for this Yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion-nature is calmed, who is sinless and of the nature of the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 27, p. 95–96

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः ।
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
yuñjannevaṃ sadā''tmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ |
sukhena brahmasaṃsparśamatyantaṃ sukhamaśnute || 28 ||
translation: The Yogî who thus, ever harmonising the self, hath put away sin, he easily enjoyeth the infinite bliss of contact with the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 28, p. 96

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani |
īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ || 29 ||
translation: The self, harmonised by yoga, seeth the Self abiding in all beings, all beings in the Self; everywhere he seeth the same.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 29, p. 96

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati |
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati || 30 ||
translation: He who seeth Me everywhere, and seeth everything in Me, of him will I never lose hold, and he shall never lose hold of Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 30, p. 96

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः ।
सर्वथा वर्त्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ |
sarvathā varttamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate || 31 ||
translation: He who, established in unity, worshippeth Me abiding in all beings, that Yogi liveth in Me, whatever his mode of living.

cross_checks.other_text:
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 31, p. 97

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन ।
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo'rjuna |
sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ || 32 ||
translation: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, seeth equality in everything, whether pleasant or painful, he is considered a perfect Yogî.

translator_notes.text: The same Self shining in the heart of each.

cross_checks.other_text:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन।
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 32, p. 97

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन ।
एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
yo'yaṃ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana |
etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvātsthitiṃ sthirām || 33 ||
translation: This yoga which Thou hast declared to be by equanimity, O Madhusûdana, I see not a stable foundation for it, owing to restlessness;

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers; speaker shown from the Sanskrit text.

cross_checks.other_text:
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन।
एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 33, p. 97

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्‌ दृढम् ।
तस्याऽहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham |
tasyā'haṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram || 34 ||
translation: For the mind is verily restless, O Krishna; it is impetuous, strong and difficult to bend. I deem it as hard to curb as the wind.

cross_checks.other_text:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 34, p. 98

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calam |
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate || 35 ||
translation: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion.

cross_checks.other_text:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 35, p. 98

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।
वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ |
vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo'vāptumupāyataḥ || 36 ||
translation: Yoga is hard to attain, methinks, by a self that is uncontrolled; but by the Self-controlled it is attainable by properly directed energy.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 36, p. 98

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः ।
अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ |
aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati || 37 ||
translation: He who is unsubdued but who possesseth faith, with the mind wandering away from yoga, failing to attain perfection in yoga, what path doth he tread, O Krishna?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 37, p. 99

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति ।
अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati |
apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi || 38 ||
translation: Fallen from both, is he destroyed like a rent cloud, unsteadfast, O mighty-armed, deluded in the path of the Eternal?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 38, p. 99

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
एतं मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः ।
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता नह्युपपद्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ |
tvadanyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā nahyupapadyate || 39 ||
translation: Deign, O Krishna, to completely dispel this doubt of mine; for there is none to be found save Thyself able to destroy this doubt.

cross_checks.other_text:
एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः।
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 39, p. 99–100

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।
न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्‌दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate |
na hi kalyāṇakṛtkaściddurgatiṃ tāta gacchati || 40 ||
translation: O son of Prithâ, neither in this world nor in the life to come is there destruction for him; never doth any who worketh righteousness, O beloved, tread the path of woe.

cross_checks.other_text:
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते।
नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 40, p. 100

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः ।
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ |
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate || 41 ||
translation: Having attained to the worlds of the pure-doing, and having dwelt there for immemorial years, he who fell from yoga is reborn in a pure and blessed house;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 41, p. 100

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् ।
एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
athavā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām |
etaddhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yadīdṛśam || 42 ||
translation: Or he may even be born into a family of wise Yogîs; but such a birth as that is most difficult to obtain in this world.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 42, p. 100–101

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् ।
यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥ ४३ ॥
transliteration:
tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam |
yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana || 43 ||
translation: There he recovereth the characteristics belonging to this former body, and with these he again laboureth for perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 43, p. 101

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः ।
जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥ ४४ ॥
transliteration:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo'pi saḥ |
jijñāsurapi yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate || 44 ||
translation: By that former practice he is irresistibly swept away. Only wishing to know yoga, even the seeker after yoga goeth beyond the Brâhmic world;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 44, p. 101

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः ।
अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ ४५ ॥
transliteration:
prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṃśuddhakilbiṣaḥ |
anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim || 45 ||
translation: But the Yogî, labouring with assiduity, purified from sin, fully perfected through manifold births, he reacheth the supreme goal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 45, p. 101–102

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः ।
कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥ ४६ ॥
transliteration:
tapasvibhyo'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo'pi mato'dhikaḥ |
karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmādyogī bhavārjuna || 46 ||
translation: The Yogî is greater than the ascetics; he is thought to be greater than even the wise; the Yogî is greater than the men of action; therefore become thou a Yogî, O Arjuna!

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 46, p. 102

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ।
श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥ ४७ ॥
transliteration:
yogināmapi sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā |
śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ || 47 ||
translation: And among all Yogîs, he who, full of faith, with the inner Self abiding in Me, adoreth Me, he is considered by Me to be the most completely harmonised.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 6, verse 47, p. 102

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः ।
असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjanmadāśrayaḥ |
asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu || 1 ||
translation: With the mind clinging to me, O Pârtha, performing yoga, refuged in Me, how thou shalt without doubt know Me to the uttermost, that hear thou.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 1, p. 103

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
jñānaṃ te'haṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ |
yajjñātvā neha bhūyo'nyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate || 2 ||
translation: I will declare to thee this knowledge and wisdom in its completeness, which, having known, there is nothing more here needeth to be known.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 2, p. 103

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaścidyatati siddhaye |
yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaścinmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ || 3 ||
translation: Among thousands of men scarce one striveth for perfection; of the successful strivers scarce one knoweth Me in essence.

cross_checks.other_text:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 3, p. 103–104

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च ।
अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhireva ca |
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā || 4 ||
translation: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, Mind, and Reason also and Egoism—these are the eightfold division of My nature.

translator_notes.text: Prakriti, matter in the widest sense of the term, including all that has extension. The "Higher Prakriti," of the next verse, is sometimes called Daivîprakriti, the Light of the Logos.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 4, p. 104

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् ।
जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
apareyamitastvanyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām |
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat || 5 ||
translation: This the inferior. Know My other nature, the higher, the life-element, O mighty-armed, by which the universe is upheld.

translator_notes.text: Prakriti, matter in the widest sense of the term, including all that has extension. The "Higher Prakriti," of the next verse, is sometimes called Daivîprakriti, the Light of the Logos.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 5, p. 104

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय ।
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya |
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā || 6 ||
translation: Know this to be the womb of all beings. I am the source of the forthgoing of the whole universe and likewise the place of its dissolving.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 6, p. 104–105

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय ।
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiñcidasti dhanañjaya |
mayi sarvamidaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva || 7 ||
translation: There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 7, p. 105

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभाऽस्मि शशिसूर्ययोः ।
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhā'smi śaśisūryayoḥ |
praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu || 8 ||
translation: I the sapidity in waters, O son of Kuntî, I the radiance in moon and sun; the Word of Power in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and virility in men;

cross_checks.other_text:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः।
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 8, p. 105

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau |
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu || 9 ||
translation: The pure fragrance of earths and the brilliance in fire am I; the life in all beings am I, and the austerity in ascetics.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 9, p. 105–106

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham || 10 ||
translation: Know Me, O Pârtha! as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the Reason of the Reason-endowed, the splendour of splendid things am I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 10, p. 106

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
balaṃ balavatāmasmi kāmarāgavivarjitam |
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha || 11 ||
translation: And I the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. In beings I am desire not contrary to duty, O Lord of the Bharatas.

cross_checks.other_text:
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम्।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 11, p. 106

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये ।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye |
matta eveti tānviddhi na tvahaṃ teṣu te mayi || 12 ||
translation: The natures that are harmonious, active, slothful, these know as from Me; not I in them, but they in me.

translator_notes.text: Sattvic, rajasic, tamasic, that is, those in whom one of the three qualities, Sattva, Rajah, Tamah, predominates.

cross_checks.other_text:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 12, p. 106

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat |
mohitaṃ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam || 13 ||
translation: All this world, deluded by these natures made by the three qualities, knoweth not Me, above these, imperishable.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 13, p. 107

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā |
māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāṃ taranti te || 14 ||
translation: This divine illusion of Mine, caused by the qualities, is hard to pierce; they who come to Me, they cross over this illusion.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 14, p. 107

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः ।
माययाऽपहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ १५॥
transliteration:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ |
māyayā'pahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ || 15||
translation: The evil-doing, the deluded, the vilest men, they come not to Me, they whose wisdom is destroyed by illusion, who have embraced the nature of demons.

translator_notes.text: Asuras, the opponents of the Suras or gods.

cross_checks.other_text:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः।
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 15, p. 107

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन ।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna |
ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha || 16 ||
translation: Fourfold in division are the righteous ones who worship me, O Arjuna; the suffering, the seeker for knowledge, the self-interested and the wise, O Lord of the Bhâratas.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 16, p. 108

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktirviśiṣyate |
priyo hi jñānino'tyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ || 17 ||
translation: Of these the wise, constantly harmonised, worshipping the One, is the best; I am supremely dear to the wise, and he is dear to Me.

cross_checks.other_text:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 17, p. 108

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् ।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam |
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim || 18 ||
translation: Noble are all these, but I hold the wise as verily Myself; he, Self united, is fixed on Me, the highest Path.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 18, p. 108

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते ।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṃ prapadyate |
vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ || 19 ||
translation: At the close of many births the man full of wisdom cometh unto Me; "Vâsudeva is all." saith he, the Mahâtmâ, very difficult to find.

translator_notes.text: A name of Shrî Krishna, as the son of Vasudeva.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 19, p. 108–109

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः ।
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ |
taṃ taṃ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā || 20 ||
translation: They whose wisdom hath been rent away by desires go forth to other Shining Ones, resorting to various external observances, according to their own natures.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 20, p. 109

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयाऽर्चितुमिच्छति ।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayā'rcitumicchati |
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham || 21 ||
translation: Any devotee who seeketh to worship with faith any such aspect, I verily bestow the unswerving faith of that man.

cross_checks.other_text:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 21, p. 109

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते ।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate |
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitānhi tān || 22 ||
translation: He endowed with that faith, seeketh the worship of such a one, and from him he obtaineth his desires, I verily decreeing the benefits;

cross_checks.other_text:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 22, p. 109–110

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् ।
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām |
devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi || 23 ||
translation: Finite indeed the fruit that belongeth to those who are of small intelligence. To the Shining Ones go the worshippers of the Shining Ones, but my devotees come unto Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 23, p. 110

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः ।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
avyaktaṃ vyaktimāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ |
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam || 24 ||
translation: Those devoid of Reason think of Me, the unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My supreme nature, imperishable, most excellent.

cross_checks.other_text:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 24, p. 110

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ |
mūḍho'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam || 25 ||
translation: Nor am I of all discovered, enveloped in My creation-illusion. This deluded world knoweth Me not, the unborn, the imperishable.

translator_notes.text: Yoga-Maya, the creative power of Yoga, all things being the thought-forms of the One.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 25, p. 110–111

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन ।
भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna |
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana || 26 ||
translation: I know the beings that are past, that are present, that are to come, O Arjuna, but no one knoweth Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 26, p. 111

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत ।
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata |
sarvabhūtāni sammohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa || 27 ||
translation: By the delusion of the pairs of opposites, sprung from attraction and repulsion, O Bhârata, all beings walk this universe wholly deluded, O Parantapa.

cross_checks.other_text:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत।
सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 27, p. 111

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
yeṣāṃ tvantagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām |
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ || 28 ||
translation: But those men of pure deeds, in whom sin is come to an end, they, freed from the delusive pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in vows.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 28, p. 111–112

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये ।
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye |
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam || 29 ||
translation: They who, refuged in Me, strive for liberation from birth and death, they know the Eternal, the whole Self-knowledge, and all action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 29, p. 112

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः ।
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ || 30 ||
translation: They who know Me as the knowledge of the elements, as that of the Shining Ones, and as that of the Sacrifice, they harmonised in mind, know Me verily even in the time of forthgoing.

translator_notes.text: These six terms are: Brahman, Adhyâtma, Karma, Adhibhûta, Adhidaiva, Adhiyajña.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 7, verse 30, p. 112

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम ।
अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
kiṃ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama |
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate || 1 ||
translation: What is that Eternal, what Self-knowledge, what Action, O Purushottama? And what is declared to be the knowledge of the Elements, what is called the knowledge of the Shining Ones?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 1, p. 114

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन ।
प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'sminmadhusūdana |
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ || 2 ||
translation: What is the knowledge of Sacrifice in this body, and how, O, Madhusûdana? And how, at the time of forthgoing art Thou known by the Self-controlled?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 2, p. 114

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate |
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ || 3 ||
translation: The indestructible, the supreme is the Eternal; His essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the emanation that causes the birth of beings is named Action;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 3, p. 115

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् ।
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam |
adhiyajño'hamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara || 4 ||
translation: Knowledge of the Elements concerns My perishable nature, and knowledge of the Shining Ones concerns the life-giving energy; the knowledge of Sacrifice tells of Me, as wearing the body, O best of living beings.

translator_notes.text: Purusha, the male creative energy. The supreme Pursha is the Divine Man, the manifested God.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 4, p. 115

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् ।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram |
yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ || 5 ||
translation: And he who, casting off the body, goeth forth thinking upon Me only at the time of the end, he entereth into My being: there is no doubt of that.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 5, p. 116

sensitivity.note: Teaching on the indestructible self, given to a warrior before battle. Never present it as making death, killing or self-harm acceptable or unimportant.

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram |
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ || 6 ||
translation: Whosoever at the end abandoneth the body, thinking upon any being, to that being only he goeth, O Kaunteya, ever to that conformed in nature.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 6, p. 116

sensitivity.note: Teaching on the indestructible self, given to a warrior before battle. Never present it as making death, killing or self-harm acceptable or unimportant.

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca |
mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṃśayam || 7 ||
translation: Therefore at all times think upon Me only and fight. With mind and Reason set on Me, without doubt thou shalt come to Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 7, p. 116

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना ।
परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā |
paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan || 8 ||
translation: With the mind not wandering after aught else, harmonised by continual practice, constantly meditating, O Pârtha, one goeth to the Spirit supreme, divine.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 8, p. 117

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः ।
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
kaviṃ purāṇamanuśāsitāramaṇoraṇīyāṃsamanusmaredyaḥ |
sarvasya dhātāramacintyarūpamādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt || 9 ||
translation: He who thinketh upon the Ancient, the Omniscient, the All-Ruler, minuter than the minute, the supporter of all, of form unimaginable, refulgent as the sun beyond the darkness,

cross_checks.other_text:
कविं पुराणमनुशासितार
मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः।
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप
मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 9, p. 117

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव ।
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
prayāṇakāle manasā'calena bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva |
bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam || 10 ||
translation: In the time of forthgoing, with unshaken mind, fixed in devotion, by the power of yoga drawing together his life-breath in the centre of the two eyebrows, he goeth to this Spirit, supreme, divine.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 10, p. 117–118

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः ।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
yadakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti viśanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ |
yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tatte padaṃ saṅgraheṇa pravakṣye || 11 ||
translation: That which is declared indestructible by the Veda-knowers, that which the controlled and passion-free enter, that desiring which Brahmacharya is performed, that path I will declare to thee with brevity.

cross_checks.other_text:
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति
विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 11, p. 118

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च ।
मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām || 12 ||
translation: All the gates closed, the mind confined in the heart, the life-breath fixed in his own head, concentrated by yoga,

translator_notes.text: The gates of the body, i.e. , the sense-organs.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 12, p. 119

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् ।
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran |
yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim || 13 ||
translation: "Aum!" the one syllabled Eternal, reciting, thinking upon Me, he who goeth forth, abandoning the body, he goeth on the highest path.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 13, p. 119

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः ।
तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ |
tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ || 14 ||
translation: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 14, p. 119

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् ।
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam |
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ || 15 ||
translation: Having come to Me, these Mahâtmâs come not again to birth, the place of pain, non-eternal; they have gone to the highest bliss.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 15, p. 120

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन ।
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna |
māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate || 16 ||
translation: The worlds, beginning with the world of Brahmâ, they come and go, O Arjuna; but he who cometh unto Me, O Kaunteya, he knoweth birth no more.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 16, p. 120

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः ।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇo viduḥ |
rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te'horātravido janāḥ || 17 ||
translation: The people who know the day of Brahmâ, a thousand ages in duration, and the night a thousand ages in ending, they know day and night.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 17, p. 120

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे ।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame |
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake || 18 ||
translation: From the unmanifested all the manifested stream forth at the coming of day; at the coming of night they dissolve, even in That called the unmanifested.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 18, p. 121

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते ।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate |
rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame || 19 ||
translation: This multitude of beings, going forth repeatedly, is dissolved at the coming of night: by ordination, O Pârtha, it streams forth at the coming of day.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 19, p. 121

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः ।
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo'vyakto'vyaktātsanātanaḥ |
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati || 20 ||
translation: Therefore verily there existeth, higher than that unmanifested, another unmanifested, eternal, which in the destroying of all beings, is not destroyed.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 20, p. 121

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् ।
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim |
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama || 21 ||
translation: That unmanifested, "the Indestructible," It is called; It is named the highest Path. They who reach It return not. That is My supreme abode.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 21, p. 122

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया ।
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā |
yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṃ tatam || 22 ||
translation: He, the highest Spirit, O Pârtha, may be reached by unswerving devotion to Him alone, in whom all beings abide, by whom all This is pervaded.

translator_notes.text: This, the universe, in opposition to that , the source of all.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 22, p. 122

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः ।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ |
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha || 23 ||
translation: That time wherein going forth Yogîs return not, and also that wherein going forth they return, that time shall I declare to thee, O prince of the Bhâratas.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 23, p. 122–123

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् ।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam |
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ || 24 ||
translation: Fire, light, day-time, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path—then, going forth, the men who know the Eternal go to the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 24, p. 123

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् ।
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam |
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate || 25 ||
translation: Smoke, night-time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path—then the Yogî, obtaining the moonlight, returneth.

translator_notes.text: The Lunar, or astral body. Until this is slain the soul returns to birth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 25, p. 123

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते ।
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate |
ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayā''vartate punaḥ || 26 ||
translation: Light and darkness, these are thought to be the world's everlasting paths; by the one he goeth who returneth not, by the other he who returneth again.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 26, p. 123–124

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन ।
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana |
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna || 27 ||
translation: Knowing these paths, O Pârtha, the Yogi is nowise perplexed. Therefore in all times be firm in yoga, O Arjuna.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 27, p. 124

division_title: The Yoga of the Indestructible Supreme Eternal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् ।
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam |
atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam || 28 ||
translation: The fruit of meritorious deeds, attached in the Vedas to sacrifices, to austerities, and also to almsgiving, the Yogî passeth all these by having known this, and goeth to the supreme and ancient Seat.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 8, verse 28, p. 124

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave |
jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt || 1 ||
translation: To thee, the uncarping, verily shall I declare this profoundest Secret, wisdom with knowledge combined, which, having known, thou shalt be freed from evil.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 1, p. 126

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ।
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam |
pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam || 2 ||
translation: Kingly Science, kingly Secret, supreme Purifier, this; intuitional, according to righteousness, very easy to perform, imperishable.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 2, p. 126

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa |
aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani || 3 ||
translation: Men without faith in this knowledge, O Parantapa, not reaching Me, return to the paths of this world of death.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 3, p. 126–127

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना ।
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
mayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā |
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ || 4 ||
translation: By Me all this world is pervaded in My unmanifested aspect; all beings have root in Me, I am not rooted in them.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 4, p. 127

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram |
bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ || 5 ||
translation: Nor have beings root in Me; behold My sovereign Yoga! The support of beings, yet not rooted in beings, My Self their efficient cause.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 5, p. 127

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
yathā''kāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān |
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya || 6 ||
translation: As the mighty air everywhere moving is rooted in the Ether, so all beings rest rooted in Me—thus know thou.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 6, p. 127

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् ।
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām |
kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham || 7 ||
translation: All beings, O Kaunteya, enter my lower nature at the end of a world-age; at the beginning of a world-age again I emanate them.

translator_notes.text: Kalpa, a period of activity, of manifestation.
Kalpa, a period of activity, of manifestation.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 7, p. 128

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ |
bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt || 8 ||
translation: Hidden in Nature, which is mine own, I emanate again and again all this multitude of beings, helpless, by the force of Nature.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 8, p. 128

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ।
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya |
udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu || 9 ||
