translation: Nor do these works bind me, O Dhananjaya, enthroned on high unattached to actions.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 9, p. 128

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् ।
हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
mayā'dhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram |
hetunā'nena kaunteya jagadviparivartate || 10 ||
translation: Under Me as supervisor, Nature sends forth the moving and unmoving: because of this, O Kaunteya, the universe revolves.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 10, p. 128–129

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् ।
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāśritam |
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram || 11 ||
translation: The foolish disregard Me, when clad in human semblance, ignorant of My supreme nature, the great Lord of beings;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 11, p. 129

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ |
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ || 12 ||
translation: Empty of hope, empty of deeds, empty of wisdom, senseless, partaking of the deceitful, brutal and demoniacal nature.

translator_notes.text: Prakriti. The Tamasic Guna, or the dark quality of Prakriti, characterises the beings here spoken of as rakshasic and asuric. Rakshasas were semi-human beings, brutal and bloodthirsty; Asuras were the opponents of the Devas.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 12, p. 129

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः ।
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ |
bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam || 13 ||
translation: Verily the Mahâtmâs, O Partha, partaking of My divine nature, worship with unwavering mind, having known Me, the imperishable source of beings.

translator_notes.text: Prakriti. The Tamasic Guna, or the dark quality of Prakriti, characterises the beings here spoken of as rakshasic and asuric. Rakshasas were semi-human beings, brutal and bloodthirsty; Asuras were the opponents of the Devas.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 13, p. 129–130

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः ।
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ |
namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate || 14 ||
translation: Always magnifying Me, strenuous, firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion ever harmonised.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 14, p. 130

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते ।
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate |
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham || 15 ||
translation: Others also, sacrificing with the sacrifice of wisdom, worship Me as the One and the Manifold everywhere present.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 15, p. 130

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् ।
मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhā'hamahamauṣadham |
mantro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam || 16 ||
translation: I the ablation; I the sacrifice; I the ancestral offering; I the fire-giving herb; the mantram I; I also the butter; I the fire; the burnt-offering I;

cross_checks.other_text:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम्।
मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 16, p. 130

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः ।
वेद्यं पवित्रमोङ्कार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
pitā'hamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
vedyaṃ pavitramoṅkāra ṛk sāma yajureva ca || 17 ||
translation: I the Father of this universe, the Mother, the Supporter, the Grandsire, the Holy one to be known, the Word of Power, and also the Rik, Sâma, and Yajur,

cross_checks.other_text:
पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः।
वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 17, p. 131

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् ।
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt |
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam || 18 ||
translation: The Path, Husband, Lord, Witness, Abode, Shelter, Lover, Origin, Dissolution, Foundation, house, Seed imperishable.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 18, p. 131

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च ।
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca |
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna || 19 ||
translation: I give heat; I hold back and send forth the rain; immortality and also death, being and non-being am I, Arjuna.

translator_notes.text: Sat and Asat, the final pair of opposites, beyond which is only the One.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 19, p. 131

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापाः यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते ।
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकमश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpāḥ yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante |
te puṇyamāsādya surendralokamaśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān || 20 ||
translation: The knowers of the three, the Soma-drinkers, the purified from sin, worshipping Me with sacrifice, pray of Me the way to heaven; they, ascending to the holy world of the Ruler of the Shining Ones, eat in heaven the divine feasts of the Shining Ones.

cross_checks.other_text:
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा
यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते।
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक
मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 20, p. 132

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालम्
क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति ।
एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्नाः
गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālam
kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti |
evaṃ trayīdharmamanuprapannāḥ
gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante || 21 ||
translation: They, having enjoyed the spacious heaven-world, their holiness withered, come back to this world of death. Following the virtues enjoined by the three, desiring desires, they obtain the transitory.

translator_notes.text: The fruit of their good deeds finished, their reward exhausted.

cross_checks.other_text:
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं
क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति।
एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना
गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 21, p. 132–133

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham || 22 ||
translation: To those men who worship Me alone thinking of no other, to those ever harmonious, I bring full security.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 22, p. 133

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः ।
तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
ye'pyanyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ |
te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam || 23 ||
translation: Even the devotees of other Shining Ones, who worship full of faith, they also worship Me, O son of Kuntî, though contrary to the ancient rule.

cross_checks.other_text:
येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।
तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 23, p. 133

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca |
na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te || 24 ||
translation: I am indeed the enjoyer of all sacrifices and also the Lord, but they know Me not in Essence, and hence they fall.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 24, p. 133–134

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः ।
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
yānti devavratā devān pitṝnyānti pitṛvratāḥ |
bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām || 25 ||
translation: They who worship the Shining Ones go to the Shining Ones; to the Ancestors go the Ancestor-worshippers; to the Elements go those who sacrifice to Elementals; but My worshippers come unto Me.

cross_checks.other_text:
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः।
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 25, p. 134

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ || 26 ||
translation: He who offereth to Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, that I accept from the striving self, offered as it is with devotion.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 26, p. 134

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् ।
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat |
yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam || 27 ||
translation: Whatsoever thou doest, whatsoever thou eatest, whatsoever thou offerest, whatsoever thou givest, whatsoever thou doest of austerity, O Kaunteya, do thou that as an offering unto Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 27, p. 134–135

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः ।
संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ |
saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi || 28 ||
translation: Thus shalt thou be liberated from the bonds of action, yielding good and evil fruits; thyself harmonised by the yoga of renunciation, thou shalt come unto Me when set free.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 28, p. 135

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ |
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham || 29 ||
translation: The same am I to all beings; there is none hateful to Me nor dear. They verily who worship Me with devotion, they are in Me, and I also in them.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 29, p. 135

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् ।
साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk |
sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ || 30 ||
translation: Even if the most sinful worship Me, with undivided heart, he too must be accounted righteous, for he hath rightly resolved;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 30, p. 135–136

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ।
कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati |
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati || 31 ||
translation: Speedily he becometh dutiful and goeth to eternal peace; O Kaunteya, know thou for certain that My devotee perisheth never.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 31, p. 136

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ |
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim || 32 ||
translation: They who take refuge with Me, O Partha, though of the womb of sin, women, Vaishyas, even Shûdras, they also tread the highest path.

translator_notes.text: The fourth, the manual labouring class.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 32, p. 136

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा ।
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā |
anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām || 33 ||
translation: How much rather then holy Brâhmanas and devoted royal saints; having obtained this transient joyless world, worship thou Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 33, p. 136–137

division_title: The Yoga of the Kingly Science and the Kingly Secret
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ || 34 ||
translation: On Me fix thy mind, be devoted to Me; sacrifice to Me; prostrate thyself before Me; harmonised thus in the Self, thou shalt come unto Me, having Me as thy supreme goal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 9, verse 34, p. 137

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
yatte'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā || 1 ||
translation: Again, O mighty-armed, hear thou My supreme word, that, desiring thy welfare, I will declare to thee who art beloved.

cross_checks.other_text:
भूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 1, p. 138

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।
अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ |
ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ || 2 ||
translation: The multitude of the Shining Ones, or the great Rishis, know not my forthcoming, for I am the beginning of all the Shining Ones and the great Rishis.

translator_notes.text: A Rishi is a man who has completed his human evolution, but who remains in the super-physical regions in touch with the earth, in order to help humanity.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 2, p. 138

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् ।
असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
yo māmajamanādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram |
asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate || 3 ||
translation: He who knoweth Me, unborn, beginningless, the great Lord of the world, he among mortals without delusion, is liberated from all sin.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 3, p. 139

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसम्मोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः ।
सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
buddhirjñānamasammohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ |
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayameva ca || 4 ||
translation: Reason, wisdom, non-illusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, existence, non-existence, fear, and also courage

cross_checks.other_text:
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः।
सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 4, p. 139

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः ।
भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṃ yaśo'yaśaḥ |
bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ || 5 ||
translation: Harmlessness, equanimity, content, austerity, almsgiving, fame and obloquy are the various characteristics of beings issuing from Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 5, p. 139

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा ।
मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā |
madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ || 6 ||
translation: The seven great Rishis, the ancient Four, and also the Manus, were born of My nature, and mind; of them this race was generated.

translator_notes.text: The four Kumaras, or Virgin Youths, the highest in the occult Hierarchy of this earth.
The heads and legislators of a race.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 6, p. 139–140

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ |
so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7 ||
translation: He who knows in essence that sovereignty and yoga of Mine, he is harmonised by unfaltering yoga; there is no doubt thereof.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 7, p. 140

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते ।
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate |
iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ || 8 ||
translation: I am the Generator of all; all evolves from Me; understanding thus, the wise adore Me in rapt emotion.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 8, p. 140

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् ।
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca || 9 ||
translation: Mindful of Me, their life hidden in Me, illumining each other, ever conversing about Me, they are content and joyful.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 9, p. 140–141

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam |
dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te || 10 ||
translation: To these, ever harmonious, worshipping in love, I give the yoga of discrimination by which they come unto Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 10, p. 141

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः ।
नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṃ tamaḥ |
nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā || 11 ||
translation: Out of pure compassion for them, dwelling within their Self, I destroy the ignorance-born darkness by the shining lamp of wisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 11, p. 141

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |
puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum || 12 ||
translation: Thou art the supreme Eternal, the supreme Abode, the supreme Purity, eternal divine man, primeval Deity, unborn, the Lord!

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 12, p. 141–142

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा ।
असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā |
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me || 13 ||
translation: All the Rishis have thus acclaimed Thee, as also the divine Rishi, Nârada; so Asita, Devala, and Vyâsa; and now Thou Thyself tellest it me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 13, p. 142

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव ।
न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
sarvametadṛtaṃ manye yanmāṃ vadasi keśava |
na hi te bhagavanvyaktiṃ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ || 14 ||
translation: All this I believe true that Thou sayest to me, O Keshava. Thy manifestation, O Blessed Lord, neither Shining Ones nor Dânavas comprehend.

cross_checks.other_text:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव।
न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 14, p. 142

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
स्वयमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम ।
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
svayamevātmanā''tmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama |
bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate || 15 ||
translation: Thyself indeed knowest Thyself by Thyself, O Purushottama; Source of beings, Lord of beings, Shining One of Shining Ones, Ruler of the world!

cross_checks.other_text:
स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम।
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 15, p. 143

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ |
yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṃstvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi || 16 ||
translation: Deign to tell without reserve of Thine own divine glories, by which glories Thou remainest, pervading these worlds.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 16, p. 143

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् ।
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
kathaṃ vidyāmahaṃ yogiṃstvāṃ sadā paricintayan |
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā || 17 ||
translation: How may I know thee, O Yogi, by constant meditation? In what, in what aspects art Thou to be thought of by me, O blessed Lord?

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 17, p. 143

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन ।
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana |
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam || 18 ||
translation: In detail tell me again of Thy yoga and glory, O Janardana; for me there is never satiety in hearing thy life-giving words.

cross_checks.other_text:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन।
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 18, p. 143–144

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः ।
प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ |
prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me || 19 ||
translation: Blessed be thou! I will declare to thee My divine glory by its chief characteristics, O best of the Kurus; there is no end to details of Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 19, p. 144

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः ।
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ |
ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca || 20 ||
translation: I, O Gudakesha, am the Self, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 20, p. 144

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् ।
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān |
marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī || 21 ||
translation: Of the Adityas I am Vishnu; of radiances the glorious sun; I am Marîchi of the Maruts; of the asterisms the Moon am I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 21, p. 144

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā || 22 ||
translation: Of the Vedas I am the Sâma-Veda; I am Vâsava of the Shining Ones; and of the senses I am the mind; I am of living beings the intelligence.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 22, p. 145

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् ।
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām |
vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham || 23 ||
translation: And of the Rudras Shañkara am I; Vittesha of the Yakshas and Râkshasas; and of the Vasus I am Pâvaka; Meru of high mountains am I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 23, p. 145

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ || 24 ||
translation: And know Me, O Pârtha, of household priests the chief, Brihaspati: of generals I am Skanda; of lakes I am the ocean.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 24, p. 145

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् ।
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram |
yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ || 25 ||
translation: Of the great Rishis Bhṛigu; of speech I am the one syllable; of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetitions; of immovable things the Himâlaya.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 25, p. 146

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः ।
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ || 26 ||
translation: Asvattha of all tree; and of divine Rishis Nârada; of Gandharvas Chitraratha; of the perfected the Muni Kapila.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 26, p. 146

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् ।
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam |
airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam || 27 ||
translation: Uchchaishravas of horses know me, nectar-born; Airâvata of lordly elephants, and of men the Monarch.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 27, p. 146

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् ।
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ || 28 ||
translation: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; of cows I am Kâmadhuk; I am Kandarpa of the progenitors; of serpents Vâsuki am I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 28, p. 147

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् ।
पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham |
pitṝṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham || 29 ||
translation: And I am Ananta of Nâgas, Varuna of sea-dwellers I; and of ancestors Aryaman; Yama of governors am I.

translator_notes.text: Serpents, who were Teachers of Wisdom.

cross_checks.other_text:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्।
पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 29, p. 147

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् ।
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham |
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro'haṃ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām || 30 ||
translation: And I am Prahlâda of Daityas; of calculators Time am I; and of wild beasts I the imperial beast; and Vainateya of birds.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 30, p. 147

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् ।
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham |
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī || 31 ||
translation: Of purifiers I am the wind; Rama of warriors I; and I am Makara of fishes; of streams the Gangâ am I.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 31, p. 148

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन ।
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṃ caivāhamarjuna |
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham || 32 ||
translation: Of creations the beginning and the ending, and also the middle am I, O Arjuna. Of sciences the science concerning the Self; the speech of orators I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 32, p. 148

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च ।
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca |
ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātā'haṃ viśvatomukhaḥ || 33 ||
translation: Of letters the letter A I am, and the duality of a compound; I also everlasting Time; I the Supporter, whose face turns everywhere.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 33, p. 148

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ।
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā || 34 ||
translation: And all-devouring Death am I, and the origin of all to come; and of feminine qualities, fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, constancy, forgiveness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 34, p. 149

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् ।
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasāmaham |
māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ || 35 ||
translation: Of hymns also Brihatsâman; Gâyatrî of metres am I; of months I am Mârgasîrsha; of seasons the flowery.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 35, p. 149

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ।
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
dyūtaṃ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham |
jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatāmaham || 36 ||
translation: I am the gambling of the cheat, and the splendour of splendid things I; I am victory, I am determination, and the truth of the truthful I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 36, p. 149

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः ।
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ || 37 ||
translation: Of the Vṛishnis Vâsudeva am I; of the Pândavas Dhananjaya; of the Sages also I am Vyâsa; of poets Ushanâ the Bard.

translator_notes.text: A family, or clan, among the Hindus.
A family, or clan, among the Hindus.

cross_checks.other_text:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः।
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 37, p. 150

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् ।
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām |
maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatāmaham || 38 ||
translation: Of rulers I am the sceptre; of those that seek victory I am statesmanship; and of secrets I am also silence; the knowledge of knowers am I.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 38, p. 150

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन ।
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tadahamarjuna |
na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram || 39 ||
translation: And whatsoever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna; nor is there aught, moving or unmoving, that may exist bereft of Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 39, p. 150

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप ।
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
nānto'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa |
eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā || 40 ||
translation: There is no end of My divine powers, O Parantapa. What has been declared is illustrative of My infinite glory.

cross_checks.other_text:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप।
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 40, p. 151

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा ।
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā |
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃ'śasambhavam || 41 ||
translation: Whatsoever is glorious, good, beautiful, and mighty, understand thou that to go forth from a fragment of My splendour.

cross_checks.other_text:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा।
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 41, p. 151

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन ।
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
athavā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna |
viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat || 42 ||
translation: But what is the knowledge of all these details to thee, O Arjuna? Having pervaded this whole universe with one fragment of Myself, I remain.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 10, verse 42, p. 151

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् ।
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam |
yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama || 1 ||
translation: This word of the supreme Secret concerning the Self, Thou hast spoken out of compassion; by this my delusion is taken away.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 1, p. 153

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā |
tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam || 2 ||
translation: The production and destruction of beings have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O Lotus-eyed, and also Thy imperishable greatness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 2, p. 153

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
एवमेतद्यथाऽऽत्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
evametadyathā''ttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara |
draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama || 3 ||
translation: O supreme Lord, even as Thou describest Thyself, O best of beings, I desire to see Thy Form omnipotent.

translator_notes.text: Ishvara, the Creator and Ruler of a Universe.

cross_checks.other_text:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 3, p. 153–154

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho |
yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānamavyayam || 4 ||
translation: If Thou thinkest that by me It can be seen, O Lord, Lord of Yoga, then show me Thine imperishable Self.

cross_checks.other_text:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो।
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 4, p. 154

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ |
nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca || 5 ||
translation: Behold, O Pârtha, a Form of Me, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, various in kind, divine, various in colours and shapes.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 5, p. 154

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा ।
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā |
bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata || 6 ||
translation: Behold the Âdityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and also the Maruts; behold many marvels never seen ere this, O Bhârata.

cross_checks.other_text:
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा।
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 6, p. 154–155

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् ।
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram |
mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyaddraṣṭumicchasi || 7 ||
translation: Here, to-day, behold the whole universe, movable and immovable, standing in one in My body, O Gudâkesha, with aught else thou desirest to see.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 7, p. 155

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā |
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram || 8 ||
translation: But verily thou art not able to behold Me with these thine eyes; the divine eye I give unto thee. Behold My sovereign Yoga.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 8, p. 155

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन् महायोगेश्वरो हरिः ।
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rājan mahāyogeśvaro hariḥ |
darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram || 9 ||
translation: Having thus spoken, O King, the great Lord of Yoga, Hari, showed to Pârtha His supreme Form as Lord.

cross_checks.other_text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः।
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 9, p. 155–156

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् ।
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam |
anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham || 10 ||
translation: With many mouths and eyes, with many visions of marvel, with many divine ornaments, with many upraised divine weapons;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 10, p. 156

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् ।
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam |
sarvāścaryamayaṃ devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham || 11 ||
translation: Wearing divine necklaces and vestures, anointed with divine unguents, the God all-marvellous, boundless, with face turned everywhere.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 11, p. 156

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता ।
यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā |
yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ || 12 ||
translation: If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out together in the sky, that might resemble the glory of that Mahâtman.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 12, p. 156–157

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा ।
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
tatraikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktamanekadhā |
apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā || 13 ||
translation: There Pândava beheld the whole universe, divided into manifold parts, standing in one in the body of the Deity of Deities.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 13, p. 157

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ |
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata || 14 ||
translation: Then he, Dhananjaya, overwhelmed with astonishment, his hair upstanding, bowed down his head to the Shining One, and with joined palms spake.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 14, p. 157

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् ।
ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
paśyāmi devāṃstava deva dehe sarvāṃstathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅghān |
brahmāṇamīśaṃ kamalāsanasthamṛṣīṃśca sarvānuragāṃśca divyān || 15 ||
translation: Within Thy Form, O God, the Gods I see, All grades of beings with distinctive marks; Brahma, the Lord, upon His lotus-throne, The Rishis all, and Serpents, the Divine.

cross_checks.other_text:
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे
सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान्।
ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ
मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 15, p. 157–158

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रम्
पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् ।
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिम्
पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
anekabāhūdaravaktranetram
paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato'nantarūpam |
nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punastavādim
paśyāmi viśveśvara viśvarūpa || 16 ||
translation: With mouths, eyes, arms, breasts multitudinous, I see Thee everywhere, unbounded Form. Beginning, middle, end, nor source of Thee, Infinite Lord, infinite Form, I find;

cross_checks.other_text:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं
पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्।
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं
पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 16, p. 158

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् ।
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद् दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca tejorāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantam |
paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ samantād dīptānalārkadyutimaprameyam || 17 ||
translation: Shining, a mass of splendour everywhere, With discus, mace, tiara, I behold: Blazing as fire, as sun dazzling the gaze, From all sides in the sky, immeasurable.

cross_checks.other_text:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च
तेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम्।
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता
द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 17, p. 158–159

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यम्
त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता
सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
tvamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyam
tvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
tvamavyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā
sanātanastvaṃ puruṣo mato me || 18 ||
translation: Lofty beyond all thought, unperishing, Thou treasure-house supreme, all-immanent; Eternal Dharma's changeless Guardian, Thou; As immemorial Man I think of Thee.

cross_checks.other_text:
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं
त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्।
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता
सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 18, p. 159

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य-
मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् ।
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya-
manantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram |
paśyāmi tvāṃ dīptahutāśavaktram
svatejasā viśvamidaṃ tapantam || 19 ||
translation: Nor source, nor midst, nor end; infinite force, Unnumbered arms, the sun and moon Thine eyes I see Thy face, as sacrificial fire Blazing, its splendour burneth up the worlds.

cross_checks.other_text:
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य
मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम्।
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 19, p. 159–160

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि
व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः ।
दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदम्
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi
vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ |
dṛṣṭvā'dbhutaṃ rūpamugraṃ tavedam
lokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman || 20 ||
translation: By Thee alone are filled the earth, the heavens, And all the regions that are stretched between; The triple worlds sink down, O mighty One, Before Thine awful manifested Form.

cross_checks.other_text:
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि
व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः।
दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 20, p. 160

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति
केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति ।
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
amī hi tvāṃ surasaṅghā viśanti
kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti |
svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ || 21 ||
translation: To Thee the troops of Suras enter in, Some with joined palms in awe invoking Thee; Banded Maharshis, Siddhas, cry: "All hail"! Chanting Thy praises with resounding songs.

cross_checks.other_text:
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्ति
केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति।
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 21, p. 160

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्याः
विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च ।
गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घाः
वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyāḥ
viśve'śvinau marutaścoṣmapāśca |
gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghāḥ
vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāścaiva sarve || 22 ||
translation: Rudras, Vasus, Sâdhyas and Adityas, Vishvas, the Ashvins, Maruts, Ushmapas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Siddhas, Asuras, In wondering multitudes beholding Thee.

translator_notes.text: Names of various grades of super-physical beings.

cross_checks.other_text:
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या
विश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च।
गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा
वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 22, p. 161

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रम्
महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् ।
बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालम्
दृष्ट्वा लोका प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम् ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetram
mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam |
bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālam
dṛṣṭvā lokā pravyathitāstathā'ham || 23 ||
translation: Thy mighty Form, with many mouths and eyes, Long armed, with thighs and feet innumerate, Vast-bosomed, set with many fearful teeth, The worlds see terror-struck, as also I.

cross_checks.other_text:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं
महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्।
बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं
दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 23, p. 161

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
नभः स्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णम्
व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् ।
दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा
धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
nabhaḥ spṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇam
vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram |
dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā
dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo || 24 ||
translation: Radiant, Thou touchest heaven, rainbow-hued, With opened mouths and shining vast-orbed eyes. My inmost self is quaking, having seen, My strength is withered, Vishnu, and my peace.

cross_checks.other_text:
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं
व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्।
दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा
धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 24, p. 162

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि
दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि ।
दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni
dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni |
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa || 25 ||
translation: Like Time's destroying flames I see Thy teeth, Upstanding, spread within expanded jaws; Nought know I anywhere, no shelter find; Mercy, O God! refuge of all the worlds!

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 25, p. 162

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः
सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः ।
भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौ
सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ |
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathā'sau
sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ || 26 ||
translation: The sons of Dhṛitarâshtra, and with them The multitude of all these kings of earth, Bhîshma, and Drona, Sûta's royal son, And all the noblest warriors of our hosts,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 26, p. 163

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति
दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि ।
केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु
संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti
daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni |
kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu
saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ || 27 ||
translation: Into Thy gaping mouths they hurrying rush, Tremendous-toothed and terrible to see; Some caught within the gaps between Thy teeth Are seen, their heads to powder crushed and ground.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 27, p. 163

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः
समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति ।
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीराः
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ
samudramevābhimukhā dravanti |
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrāḥ
viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti || 28 ||
translation: As river-floods impetuously rush, Hurling their waters into ocean's lap, So fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths, In haste, these mighty men, these lords of earth.

cross_checks.other_text:
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः
समुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति।
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 28, p. 164

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गाः
विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः ।
तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका-
स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgāḥ
viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ |
tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā-
stavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ || 29 ||
translation: As moths with quickened speed will headlong fly Into a flaming light, to fall destroyed, So also these, in haste precipitate, Enter within Thy mouths destroyed to fall.

cross_checks.other_text:
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा
विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः।
तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका
स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 29, p. 164

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता-
ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः ।
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रम्
भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā-
llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ |
tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagram
bhāsastavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo || 30 ||
translation: On every side, all-swallowing, fiery-tongued, Thou lickest up mankind, devouring all; The glory filleth space: the universe Is burning, Vishnu, with Thy blazing rays.

cross_checks.other_text:
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता
ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः।
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं
भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 30, p. 165

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो
नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद ।
विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यम्
न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo
namo'stu te devavara prasīda |
vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyam
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim || 31 ||
translation: Reveal Thy Self; what awful Form art Thou? I worship Thee! Have mercy, God supreme! Thine inner Being I am fain to know; This Thy forth-streaming Life bewilders me.

cross_checks.other_text:
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो
नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद।
विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं
न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 31, p. 165

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः ।
ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ |
ṛte'pi tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti sarve ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ || 32 ||
translation: Time am I, laying desolate the world, Made manifest on earth to slay mankind! Not one of all these warriors ranged for strife Escapeth death; thou shalt alone survive.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 32, p. 166

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् ।
मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva jitvā śatrūnbhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham |
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin || 33 ||
translation: Therefore stand up! win for thyself renown, Conquer thy foes, enjoy the wealth filled realm, By Me they are already overcome, Be thou the outward cause, left-handed one.

cross_checks.other_text:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व
जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्।
मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव
निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 33, p. 166

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान् ।
मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठाः युद्ध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca karṇaṃ tathā'nyānapi yodhavīrān |
mayā hatāṃstvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ yuddhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān || 34 ||
translation: Drona and Bhîshma and Jayadratha, Karna, and all the other warriors here, Are slain by Me. Destroy them fearlessly. Fight! thou shalt crush thy rivals in the field.

cross_checks.other_text:
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान्।
मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा
युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 34, p. 167

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य
कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी ।
नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णम्
सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
etacchrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya
kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī |
namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇam
sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya || 35 ||
translation: Having heard these words of Keshava, he who weareth a diadem, with joined palms, quaking and prostrating himself, spake again to Krishna, stammering with fear, casting down his face.

cross_checks.other_text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य
कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी।
नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं
सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 35, p. 167–168

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च ।
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā jagatprahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca |
rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ || 36 ||
translation: Hrishîkesha! in Thy magnificence Rightly the world rejoiceth, hymning Thee; The Râkshasas to every quarter fly In fear; the hosts of Siddhas prostrate fall.

cross_checks.other_text:
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या
जगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च।
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति
सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 36, p. 168

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन् गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे ।
अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
kasmācca te na nameranmahātman garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre |
ananta deveśa jagannivāsa tvamakṣaraṃ sadasattatparaṃ yat || 37 ||
translation: How should they otherwise, O loftiest Self! First Cause! Brahmâ Himself less great than Thou. Infinite, God of Gods, home of all worlds, Unperishing, Sat, Asat, That supreme!

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 37, p. 168–169

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् ।
वेत्ताऽसि वेद्यं च परं च धाम त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇastvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
vettā'si vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma tvayā tataṃ viśvamanantarūpa || 38 ||
translation: First of the Gods, most ancient Man Thou art. Supreme receptacle of all that lives; Knower and known, the dwelling-place on high; In Thy vast Form the universe is spread.

cross_checks.other_text:
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण
स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्।
वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 38, p. 169

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च ।
नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ prajāpatistvaṃ prapitāmahaśca |
namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste || 39 ||
translation: Thou art Vâyu and Yama, Agni, moon, Varuna, Father, Grandsire of all; Hail, hail to Thee! a thousand times all hail! Hail unto Thee! again, again all hail!

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 39, p. 169–170

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व ।
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वम्
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste
namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
anantavīryāmitavikramastvam
sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ || 40 ||
translation: Prostrate in front of Thee, prostrate behind; Prostrate on every side to Thee, O All. In power boundless, measureless in strength, Thou holdest all: then Thou Thyself art All.

cross_checks.other_text:
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व।
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 40, p. 170

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तम्
हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति ।
अजानता महिमानं तवेदम्
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktam
he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti |
ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedam
mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi || 41 ||
translation: If, thinking Thee but friend, importunate, O Krishna! or O Yâdava! O friend! I cried, unknowing of Thy majesty, And careless in the fondness of my love;

cross_checks.other_text:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं
हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति।
अजानता महिमानं तवेदं
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 41, p. 170–171

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु ।
एकोऽथवाऽप्यच्युत तत्समक्षम्
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si
vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu |
eko'thavā'pyacyuta tatsamakṣam
tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam || 42 ||
translation: If jesting I irreverence showed to Thee, At play, reposing, sitting or at meals, Alone, O sinless One, or with my friends, Forgive my error, O Thou boundless One.

cross_checks.other_text:
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु।
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 42, p. 171

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
पिताऽसि लोकस्य चराचरस्य
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् ।
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभावः ॥ ४३ ॥
transliteration:
pitā'si lokasya carācarasya
tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān |
na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo
lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāvaḥ || 43 ||
translation: Father of worlds, of all that moves and stands, Worthier of reverence than the Guru's self, There is none like to Thee. Who passeth Thee? Pre-eminent Thy power in all the worlds.

cross_checks.other_text:
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान्।
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 43, p. 171–172

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायम्
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् ।
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥ ४४ ॥
transliteration:
tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyam
prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam |
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum || 44 ||
translation: Therefore I fall before Thee; with my body I worship as it fitting; bless Thou me. As father with the son, as friend with friend, With the beloved as lover, bear with me.

cross_checks.other_text:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम्।
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 44, p. 172

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे ।
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपम्
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥ ४५ ॥
transliteration:
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā
bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
tadeva me darśaya deva rūpam
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa || 45 ||
translation: I have seen that which none hath seen before, My heart is glad, yet faileth me for fear; Show me, O God, Thine other Form again— Mercy, O God of Gods, home of all worlds—

cross_checks.other_text:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे।
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 45, p. 172

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तमिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव ।
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥ ४६ ॥
transliteration:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahastamicchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭumahaṃ tathaiva |
tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte || 46 ||
translation: Diademed, mace and discus in Thy hand. Again I fain would see Thee as before; Put on again Thy four-armed shape, O Lord, O thousand-armed, of forms innumerate.

cross_checks.other_text:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव।
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 46, p. 173

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदम्
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् ।
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यम्
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥ ४७ ॥
transliteration:
mayā prasannena tavārjunedam
rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt |
tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyam
yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam || 47 ||
translation: Arjuna, by My favour thou hast seen, This loftiest Form by yoga's self revealed! Radiant, all-penetrating, endless, first, That none except thyself hath ever seen.

cross_checks.other_text:
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात्।
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 47, p. 173–174

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः ।
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥ ४८ ॥
transliteration:
na vedayajñādhyayanairna dānairna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ |
evaṃrūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛloke draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra || 48 ||
translation: Nor sacrifice, nor Vedas, alms, nor works, Nor sharp austerity, nor study deep, Can win the vision of this Form for man, Foremost of Kurus, thou alone hast seen.

cross_checks.other_text:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै
र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः।
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके
द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 48, p. 174

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् ।
व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वम्
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥ ४९ ॥
transliteration:
mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo
dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramīdṛṅmamedam |
vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvam
tadeva me rūpamidaṃ prapaśya || 49 ||
translation: Be not bewildered, be thou not afraid, Because thou hast beheld this awful Form; Cast fear away, and let thy heart rejoice; Behold again Mine own familiar shape.

cross_checks.other_text:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम्।
व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 49, p. 174

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः ।
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनम्
भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥ ५० ॥
transliteration:
ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā
svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ |
āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenam
bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā || 50 ||
translation: Vâsudeva, having thus spoken to Arjuna, again manifested His own Form, and consoled the terrified one, the Mahâtman again assuming a gentle form.

cross_checks.other_text:
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः।
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं
भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 50, p. 175

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन ।
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥ ५१ ॥
transliteration:
dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana |
idānīmasmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ || 51 ||
translation: Beholding again Thy gentle human Form, O Janârdana, I am now collected, and am restored to my own nature.

cross_checks.other_text:
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन।
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 51, p. 175

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम ।
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ ५२ ॥
transliteration:
sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama |
devā apyasya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ || 52 ||
translation: This Form of Mine beholden by thee is very hard to see. Verily the Shining Ones ever long to behold this form.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 52, p. 176

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥ ५३ ॥
transliteration:
nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā |
śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā || 53 ||
translation: Nor can I be seen as thou hast seen Me by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by alms, or by offerings;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 53, p. 176

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप ॥ ५४ ॥
transliteration:
bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya ahamevaṃvidho'rjuna |
jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa || 54 ||
translation: But by devotion to Me alone I may thus be perceived, Arjuna, and known and seen in essence, and entered, O Parantapa.

cross_checks.other_text:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन।
ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 54, p. 176

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः ।
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥ ५५ ॥
transliteration:
matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ |
nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava || 55 ||
translation: He who doeth actions for Me, whose supreme good I am, My devotee, freed from attachment without hatred of any being, he cometh unto Me, O Pândava.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 11, verse 55, p. 177

speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate |
ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ || 1 ||
translation: Those devotees who ever harmonised worship Thee, and those also who worship the Indestructible, the Unmanifested, whether of these is the more learned in yoga?

corrections.basis: Flagged [sic] by Wikisource transcribers; printed reading kept (no correction suggested).

cross_checks.other_text: एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 1, p. 178

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate |
śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ || 2 ||
translation: They who with mind fixed on Me ever harmonised worship Me, with faith supreme endowed, these, in My opinion, are best in yoga.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 2, p. 178

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते ।
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam || 3 ||
translation: They who worship the Indestructible, the Ineffable, the unmanifested, Omnipresent, and Unthinkable, the Unchanging, Immutable, Eternal,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 3, p. 179

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ |
te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ || 4 ||
translation: Restraining and subduing the senses, regarding everything equally, in the welfare of all rejoicing, these also come unto Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 4, p. 179

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām |
avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate || 5 ||
translation: The difficulty of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifested is greater; for the path of the Unmanifested is hard for the embodied to reach.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 5, p. 179

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।
अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ |
