ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate || 6 ||
translation: Those verily who, renouncing all actions in Me and intent on Me, worship meditating on Me, with whole-hearted yoga,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 6, p. 180

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् ।
भवामि न चिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt |
bhavāmi na cirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām || 7 ||
translation: These I speedily lift up from the ocean of death and existence, O Pârtha, their minds being fixed on Me.

cross_checks.other_text: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात्।भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 7, p. 180

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya |
nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 8 ||
translation: Place thy mind in me, into Me let thy Reason enter; then without doubt thou shalt abide in Me hereafter.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 8, p. 180

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṃ dhanañjaya || 9 ||
translation: And if thou art not able firmly to fix thy mind on Me, then by the yoga of practice seek to reach Me, O Dhananjaya.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 9, p. 180–181

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव ।
मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava |
madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvansiddhimavāpsyasi || 10 ||
translation: If also thou art not equal to constant practice, be intent on My service; performing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.

cross_checks.other_text: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव।मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 10, p. 181

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāśritaḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān || 11 ||
translation: If even to do this thou hast not strength, then, taking refuge in union with Me, renounce all fruit of action with the self controlled.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 11, p. 181

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram || 12 ||
translation: Better indeed is wisdom than constant-practice; than wisdom, meditation is better; than meditation, renunciation of the fruit of action; on renunciation follows peace.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 12, p. 181–182

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī || 13 ||
translation: He who beareth no ill-will to any being, friendly and compassionate, without attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 13, p. 182

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मे भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
santuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ |
mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo me bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 14 ||
translation: Ever content, harmonious, with the self-controlled, resolute, with mind and Reason dedicated to Me, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.

cross_checks.other_text: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः।मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 14, p. 182

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ |
harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ || 15 ||
translation: He from whom the world doth not shrink away, who doth not shrink away from the world, freed from the anxieties of joy, anger, and fear, he is dear to me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 15, p. 182–183

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 16 ||
translation: He who wants nothing, is pure, expert, passionless, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 16, p. 183

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 17 ||
translation: He who neither loveth nor hateth, nor grieveth, nor desireth, renouncing good and evil, full of devotion, he is dear to Me.

cross_checks.other_text: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 17, p. 183

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ |
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ || 18 ||
translation: Alike to foe and friend, and also in fame and ignominy, alike in cold and heat, pleasures and pains, destitute of attachment,

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 18, p. 183–184

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् ।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yenakenacit |
aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ || 19 ||
translation: Taking equally praise and reproach, silent, wholly content with what cometh, homeless, firm in mind, full of devotion, that man is dear to Me.

cross_checks.other_text: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 19, p. 184

speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते ।
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate |
śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ || 20 ||
translation: They verily who partake of this life-giving wisdom as taught herein, endued with faith, I their supreme Object, devotees, they are surpassingly dear to Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 12, verse 20, p. 184

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च ।
एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca |
etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca keśava || 1 ||
translation: Matter and Spirit, even the Field and the Knower of the Field, wisdom and that which ought to be known, these I fain would learn, O Keshava.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 1, p. 186

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate |
etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ || 2 ||
translation: This body, son of Kuntî, is called the Field; that which knoweth it is called the Knower of the Field by the Sages.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 2, p. 186

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata |
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama || 3 ||
translation: Understand Me as the Knower of the Field in all Fields, O Bhârata. Wisdom as to the Field and the Knower of the Field, that in My opinion is the wisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 3, p. 187

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataśca yat |
sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śṛṇu || 4 ||
translation: What that Field is and of what nature, how modified, and whence it is, and what He is and what His powers, hear that now briefly from Me.

translator_notes.text: Kshetrajña, the Knower of the Field.

cross_checks.other_text: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 4, p. 187

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् ।
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak |
brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniścitaiḥ || 5 ||
translation: Rishis have sung in manifold ways, in many various chants, and in decisive Brahma-sûtra verses full of reasonings.

translator_notes.text: Short terse sayings, concerning the Eternal .

cross_checks.other_text: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक्।ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 5, p. 187

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च ।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca |
indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ || 6 ||
translation: The great Elements, Individuality, Reason, and also the unmanifested, the ten senses and the one, and the five pastures of the senses;

translator_notes.text: The five organs of knowledge, or senses, the five organs of action, the mind, and the object cognised by each of the five senses.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 6, p. 188

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः ।
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanā dhṛtiḥ |
etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam || 7 ||
translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, combination, intelligence, firmness; these, briefly described, constitute the Field and its modifications.

cross_checks.other_text: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः।एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 7, p. 188

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् ।
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam |
ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ || 8 ||
translation: Humility, unpretentiousness, harmlessness, forgiveness, rectitude, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 8, p. 188–189

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च ।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca |
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam || 9 ||
translation: Dispassion towards the objects of the senses, and also absence of egoism, insight into the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and sickness,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 9, p. 189

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु ।
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
asaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu |
nityaṃ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu || 10 ||
translation: Unattachment, absence of self-identification with son, wife or home, and constant balance of mind in wished-for and unwished-for events,

cross_checks.other_text: असक्ितरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु।नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 10, p. 189

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī |
viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi || 11 ||
translation: Unflinching devotion to Me by yoga, without other objects, resort to sequestered places, absence of enjoyment in the company of men,

cross_checks.other_text: मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्ितरव्यभिचारिणी।विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 11, p. 189–190

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् ।
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam |
etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadato'nyathā || 12 ||
translation: Constancy in the wisdom of the Self, understanding of the object of essential wisdom; that is declared to be the Wisdom; all against it is ignorance.

cross_checks.other_text: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोन्यथा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 12, p. 190

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते ।
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā'mṛtamaśnute |
anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate || 13 ||
translation: I will declare that which ought to be known, that which being known immortality is enjoyed—the beginningless supreme Eternal, called neither being nor non-being.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 13, p. 190

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ।
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham |
sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati || 14 ||
translation: Everywhere That hath hands and feet, everywhere eyes, heads, and mouths; all-hearing, He dwelleth in the world, enveloping all,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 14, p. 190–191

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् ।
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam |
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca || 15 ||
translation: Shining with all sense-faculties without any senses; unattached supporting everything and free from qualities enjoying qualities;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 15, p. 191

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च ।
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca |
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat || 16 ||
translation: Without and within all beings, immovable and also movable; by reason of His subtlety imperceptible; at hand and far away is That.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 16, p. 191

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam |
bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca || 17 ||
translation: Not divided amid beings, and yet seated distributively; that is to be known as the supporter of beings; He devours and He generates.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 17, p. 191–192

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते ।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya dhiṣṭhitam || 18 ||
translation: That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness; Wisdom, the Object of Wisdom, by Wisdom to be reached, seated in the hearts of all.

cross_checks.other_text: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 18, p. 192

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate || 19 ||
translation: Thus the Field, Wisdom and the Object of Wisdom, have been briefly told. My devotee, thus knowing, enters into My Being.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 19, p. 192

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि ।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi |
vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān || 20 ||
translation: Know thou that Matter and Spirit are both without beginning; and know thou also that modifications and qualities are all Matter-born.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 20, p. 192–193

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate |
puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate || 21 ||
translation: Matter is called the cause of the generation of causes and effects; Spirit is called the cause of the enjoyment of pleasure and pain.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 21, p. 193

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्‌क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् ।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān |
kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu || 22 ||
translation: Spirit seated in Matter useth the qualities born of Matter; attachment to the qualities is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs.

cross_checks.other_text: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 22, p. 193

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः ।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
upadraṣṭā'numantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |
paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ || 23 ||
translation: Supervisor and permitter, supporter, enjoyer, the great Lord, and also the supreme Self; thus is styled in this body the supreme Spirit.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 23, p. 193–194

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha |
sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate || 24 ||
translation: He who thus knoweth Spirit and Matter with its qualities, in whatsoever condition he may be, he shall not be born again.

cross_checks.other_text: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह।सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 24, p. 194

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना ।
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā |
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare || 25 ||
translation: Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the Self; others by the Sânkhya Yoga, and others by the Yoga of Action;

cross_checks.other_text: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 25, p. 194

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते ।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvā'nyebhya upāsate |
te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ || 26 ||
translation: Others also, ignorant of this, having heard of it from others, worship; and these also cross beyond death, adhering to what they had heard.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 26, p. 194–195

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
yāvatsañjāyate kiñcitsattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam |
kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha || 27 ||
translation: Whatsoever creature is born immobile or mobile, know thou, O best of the Bhâratas, that it is from the union between the Field and the Knower of the Field.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 27, p. 195

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram |
vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati || 28 ||
translation: Seated equally in all beings, the supreme Lord, unperishing within the perishing—he who thus seeth, he seeth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 28, p. 195

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् ।
न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
samaṃ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram |
na hinastyātmanā''tmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim || 29 ||
translation: Seeing indeed everywhere the same Lord equally dwelling, he doth not destroy the Self, and thus treads the highest Path.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 29, p. 195

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः ।
यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
yaḥ paśyati tathā''tmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati || 30 ||
translation: He who seeth that Matter verily performeth all actions, and that the Self is actionless, he seeth.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 30, p. 196

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति ।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati |
tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā || 31 ||
translation: When he perceiveth the diversified existence of beings as rooted in One, and spreading forth from it, then he reacheth the Eternal

cross_checks.other_text: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 31, p. 196

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्माऽयमव्ययः ।
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmā'yamavyayaḥ |
śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate || 32 ||
translation: Being beginningless and without qualities, the imperishable supreme Self, though seated in the body, O Kaunteya, worketh not nor is affected.

cross_checks.other_text: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 32, p. 196

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate |
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathā''tmā nopalipyate || 33 ||
translation: As the omnipresent ether is not affected, by reason of its subtlety, so seated everywhere in the body the Self is not affected.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 33, p. 197

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः ।
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ |
kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata || 34 ||
translation: As the one sun illumineth the whole earth, so the Lord of the Field illumineth the whole Field, O Bhârata.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 34, p. 197

division_title: The Yoga of the Distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā |
bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param || 35 ||
translation: They who by the eyes of Wisdom perceive this difference between the Field and the Knower of the Field, and the liberation of beings from Matter they go to the Supreme.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 13, verse 35, p. 197

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam |
yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ || 1 ||
translation: I will again proclaim that supreme Wisdom, of all wisdom the best, which having known, all the Sages have gone hence to the supreme Perfection.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 1, p. 199

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः ।
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ |
sarge'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca || 2 ||
translation: Having taken refuge in this Wisdom and being assimilated to My own nature, they are not re-born even in the emanation of a universe, nor are disquieted in the dissolution.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 2, p. 199

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् ।
सम्भवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmyaham |
sambhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata || 3 ||
translation: My womb is the great Eternal; in that I place the germ; thence cometh the birth of all beings, O Bhârata.

cross_checks.other_text: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम्।संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 3, p. 199–200

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः संभवन्ति याः ।
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
tāsāṃ brahma mahadyonirahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā || 4 ||
translation: In whatsoever wombs mortals are produced, O Kaunteya, the great Eternal is their womb, I their generating father.

cross_checks.other_text: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 4, p. 200

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ।
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam || 5 ||
translation: Harmony, Motion, Inertia, such are the qualities, Matter-born; they bind fast in the body, O great-armed one, the indestructible dweller in the body.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 5, p. 200

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam |
sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha || 6 ||
translation: Of these Harmony from its stainlessness, luminous and healthy, bindeth by the attachment to bliss and the attachment to wisdom, O sinless one.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 6, p. 200–201

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam |
tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam || 7 ||
translation: Motion, the passion nature, know thou, is the source of attachment and thirst for life, O Kaunteya, that bindeth the dweller in the body by the attachment to action.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 7, p. 201

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām |
pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata || 8 ||
translation: But Inertia, know thou, born of unwisdom, is the deluder of all dwellers in the body; that bindeth by heedlessness, indolence and sloth, O Bhârata.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 8, p. 201

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayatyuta || 9 ||
translation: Harmony attacheth to bliss, Motion to action O Bhârata. Inertia, verily, having shrouded wisdom, attacheth on the contrary to heedlessness.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 9, p. 201–202

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत ।
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā || 10 ||
translation: Now Harmony prevaileth, having overpowered Motion and Inertia, O Bhârata; now Motion, having overpowered Harmony and Inertia; and now Inertia, having overpowered Harmony and Motion.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 10, p. 202

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते ।
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśa upajāyate |
jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyādvivṛddhaṃ sattvamityuta || 11 ||
translation: When the wisdom-light streameth forth from all the gates of the body, then it may be known that Harmony is increasing.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 11, p. 202

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारंभः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
lobhaḥ pravṛttirāraṃbhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaḥ spṛhā |
rajasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha || 12 ||
translation: Greed, outgoing energy, undertaking of actions, restlessness, desire—these are born of the increase of Motion, O best of the Bhâratas.

cross_checks.other_text: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 12, p. 202–203

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca |
tamasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana || 13 ||
translation: Darkness, stagnation and heedlessness and also delusion—these are born of the increase of Inertia, O joy of the Kurus.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 13, p. 203

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt |
tadottamavidāṃ lokānamalānpratipadyate || 14 ||
translation: If Harmony verily prevaileth when the embodied goeth to dissolution, then he goeth forth to the spotless worlds of the great Sages.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 14, p. 203

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते ।
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate |
tathā pralīnastamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate || 15 ||
translation: Having gone to dissolution in Motion, he is born among those attached to action; if dissolved in Inertia, he is born in the wombs of the senseless.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 15, p. 203

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् ।
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam |
rajasastu phalaṃ duḥkhamajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam || 16 ||
translation: It is said the fruit of a good action is harmonious and spotless; verily the fruit of Motion is pain, and the fruit of Inertia unwisdom.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 16, p. 204

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca |
pramādamohau tamaso bhavato'jñānameva ca || 17 ||
translation: From Harmony wisdom is born, and also greed from Motion; heedlessness and delusion are of Inertia and also unwisdom.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 17, p. 204

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ |
jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ || 18 ||
translation: They rise upwards who are settled in Harmony; the Active dwell in the mid-most place: the Inert go downwards, enveloped in the vilest qualities.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 18, p. 204

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टाऽनुपश्यति ।
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭā'nupaśyati |
guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati || 19 ||
translation: When the Seer perceiveth no agent other than the qualities, and knoweth That which is higher than the qualities, he entereth into My Nature.

cross_checks.other_text: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 19, p. 205

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।
जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān |
janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute || 20 ||
translation: When the dweller in the body hath crossed over these three qualities, whence all bodies have been produced, liberated from birth, death, old age and sorrow, he drinketh the nectar of immortality.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 20, p. 205

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो ।
किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
kairliṅgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho |
kimācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate || 21 ||
translation: What are the marks of him who hath crossed over the three qualities, O Lord? How acteth he, and how doth he go beyond these three qualities?

cross_checks.other_text: कैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 21, p. 205–206

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।
न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava |
na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati || 22 ||
translation: He, O Pândava, who hateth not radiance, nor outgoing energy, nor even delusion, when present, nor longeth after them, absent;

cross_checks.other_text: प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 22, p. 206

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते ।
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate |
guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate || 23 ||
translation: He who, seated as a neutral, is unshaken by the qualities; who, saying, "The qualities revolve," standeth apart immovable.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 23, p. 206

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ |
tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ || 24 ||
translation: Balanced in pleasure and pain, self-reliant, to whom a lump of earth, a rock and gold are alike, the same to loved and unloved, firm, the same in censure and in praise,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 24, p. 207

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।
सर्वारंभपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ |
sarvāraṃbhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate || 25 ||
translation: The same in honour and ignominy, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings—he is said to have crossed over the qualities.

cross_checks.other_text: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 25, p. 207

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate |
sa guṇānsamatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate || 26 ||
translation: And he who serveth Me exclusively by the Yoga of devotion, he, crossing beyond the qualities, he is fit to become the Eternal.

cross_checks.other_text: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते।स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 26, p. 207

division_title: The Yoga of Separation from the Three Qualities
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhā'hamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca |
śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca || 27 ||
translation: For I am the abode of the Eternal, and of the indestructible nectar of immortality, of immemorial righteousness, and of unending bliss.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 14, verse 27, p. 208

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit || 1 ||
translation: With roots above, branches below, the Asvattha is said to be indestructible; the leaves of it are hymns; he who knoweth it is a Veda-knower.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 1, p. 209

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखाः गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtāstasya śākhāḥ guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ |
adhaśca mūlānyanusantatāni karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke || 2 ||
translation: Downwards and upwards spread the branches of it, nourished by the qualities; the objects of the senses its buds; and its roots grow downwards, the bonds of action in the world of men.

cross_checks.other_text: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः।अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 2, p. 209–210

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा ।
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलमसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādirna ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |
aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūlamasaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā || 3 ||
translation: Nor here may be acquired knowledge of its form, nor its end, nor its origin, nor its rooting-place; this strongly rooted Asvattha having been cut down by the unswerving weapon of non-attachment,

cross_checks.other_text: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा।अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 3, p. 210

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यम्
यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः ।
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये
यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyam
yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye
yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī || 4 ||
translation: That path beyond may be sought, treading which there is no return. I go indeed to that Primal Man, whence the ancient energy forth-streamed.

cross_checks.other_text: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 4, p. 210–211

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषाः
अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै-
र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣāḥ
adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ |
dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñai-
rgacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat || 5 ||
translation: Without pride and delusion, victorious over the vice of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, desire pacified, liberated from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, they tread, undeluded, that indestructible path.

cross_checks.other_text: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः।द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 5, p. 211

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama || 6 ||
translation: Nor doth the sun lighten there, nor moon, nor fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 6, p. 211

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati || 7 ||
translation: A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit, draweth round itself the senses of which the mind is the sixth, veiled in matter.

translator_notes.text: Jîva, a life, individualised from the Universal Spirit.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 7, p. 212

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।
गृहित्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ |
gṛhitvaitāni saṃyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt || 8 ||
translation: When the Lord acquireth a body and when He abandoneth it, He seizeth these and goeth with them, as the wind takes fragrances from their retreats.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

cross_checks.other_text: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः।गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 8, p. 212

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate || 9 ||
translation: Enshrined in the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste and the smell, and in the mind also, He enjoyeth the objects of the senses.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 9, p. 212

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam |
vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ || 10 ||
translation: The deluded do not perceive (Him) when He departeth or stayeth or enjoyeth, swayed by the qualities; the wisdom-eyed perceive.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 10, p. 213

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
yatanto yoginaścainaṃ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam |
yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyantyacetasaḥ || 11 ||
translation: Yogîs also, struggling, perceive Him, established in the Self; but though struggling, the unintelligent perceive Him not, their selves untrained.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 11, p. 213

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ।
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam |
yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam || 12 ||
translation: That splendour issuing from the sun that enlighteneth the whole world, that which is in the moon and in fire, that splendour know as from Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 12, p. 213

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा ।
पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā |
puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ || 13 ||
translation: Permeating the soil, I support beings by my vital energy, and having become the delicious Soma I nourish all plants.

translator_notes.text: "Having become the watery moon" is the accepted translation. Soma is a liquid, drawn from the Soma-plant. "Having become sap" is a probable translation.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 13, p. 214

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः ।
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ |
prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham || 14 ||
translation: I, having become the Fire of Life, take possession of the bodies of breathing things, and united with the life-breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 14, p. 214

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च ।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca |
vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham || 15 ||
translation: And I am seated in the hearts of all, and from Me memory and wisdom and their absence. And that which is to be known in all the Vedas am I; and I indeed the Veda-knower and the author of the Vedanta.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 15, p. 214–215

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca |
kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate || 16 ||
translation: There are two Energies in this world, the destructible and the indestructible; the destructible is all beings, the unchanging is called the indestructible.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 16, p. 215

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ |
yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ || 17 ||
translation: The highest Energy is verily Another, declared as the Supreme Self, He who, pervading all, sustaineth the three worlds, the indestructible Lord.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 17, p. 215

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ |
ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ || 18 ||
translation: Since I excel the destructible, and am more excellent also than the indestructible, in the world and in the Veda I am proclaimed the Supreme Spirit.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 18, p. 216

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
yo māmevamasaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam |
sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata || 19 ||
translation: He who undeluded knoweth Me thus as the Supreme Spirit, he, all-knowing, worshippeth Me with his whole being, O Bhârata.

cross_checks.other_text: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 19, p. 216

division_title: The Yoga of Attaining the Supreme Spirit
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ ।
एतद्‌बुध्वा बुद्धिमान् स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayā'nagha |
etadbudhvā buddhimān syātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata || 20 ||
translation: Thus by Me this most secret teaching hath been told O sinless one. This known, he hath become illuminated and hath finished his work, O Bhârata.

cross_checks.other_text: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ।एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 15, verse 20, p. 216

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam || 1 ||
translation: Fearlessness, cleanness of life, steadfastness in the Yoga of wisdom, almsgiving, self-restraint and sacrifice and study of the Scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness,

cross_checks.other_text:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 1, p. 218

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam || 2 ||
translation: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion to living beings, uncovetousness, mildness, modesty, absence of fickleness,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 2, p. 218

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā |
bhavanti sampadaṃ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata || 3 ||
translation: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of envy and pride—these are his who is born with the divine properties, O Bhârata.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 3, p. 218–219

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca |
ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha sampadamāsurīm || 4 ||
translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit, wrath and also harshness and unwisdom are his who is born, O Pârtha, with demoniacal properties.

translator_notes.text: Asuric; the Asuras were the enemies of the Suras or Gods.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 4, p. 219

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।
मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
daivī sampadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
mā śucaḥ sampadaṃ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava || 5 ||
translation: The divine properties are deemed to be for liberation, the demoniacal for bondage. Grieve not, thou art born with divine properties, O Pândava.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 5, p. 219

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
dvau bhūtasargau loke'smindaiva āsura eva ca |
daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu || 6 ||
translation: Twofold is the animal creation in this world, the divine and the demoniacal: the divine hath been described at length: hear from Me, O Pârtha, the demoniacal.

cross_checks.other_text: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 6, p. 219–220

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ |
na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate || 7 ||
translation: Demoniacal men know neither right energy nor right abstinence; nor purity, nor even propriety, nor truth is in them.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 7, p. 220

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।
अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram |
aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam || 8 ||
translation: "The universe is without truth, without basis," they say, "without a God; brought about by mutual union, and caused by lust and nothing else."

translator_notes.text: Isvara; the ruler of a universe.

cross_checks.other_text: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम्।अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 8, p. 220

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एतव दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
etava dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ |
prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ || 9 ||
translation: Holding this view, these ruined selves of small understanding, of fierce deeds, come forth as enemies for the destruction of the world.

cross_checks.other_text: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः।प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 9, p. 220–221

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।
मोहाद्‌गृहीत्वाऽसद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ |
mohādgṛhītvā'sadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ || 10 ||
translation: Surrendering themselves to insatiable desires, possessed with vanity, conceit and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they engage in action with impure resolves.

cross_checks.other_text: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः।मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 10, p. 221

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ |
kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ || 11 ||
translation: Giving themselves over to unmeasured thought whose end is death, regarding the gratification of desires as the highest, feeling sure that this is all,

cross_checks.other_text: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः।कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 11, p. 221

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān || 12 ||
translation: Held in bondage by a hundred ties of expectation, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards of wealth for sensual enjoyments.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 12, p. 222

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham |
idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam || 13 ||
translation: "This to-day by me hath been won, that purpose I shall gain; this wealth is mine already, and also this shall be mine in future.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 13, p. 222

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi |
īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī || 14 ||
translation: "I have slain this enemy, and others also I shall slay. I am the Lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful, happy;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 14, p. 222

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ || 15 ||
translation: "I am wealthy, well-born; what other is there that is like unto me? I will sacrifice, I will give alms, I will rejoice." Thus deluded by unwisdom,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 15, p. 222–223

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau || 16 ||
translation: Bewildered by numerous thoughts, enmeshed in the web of delusion, addicted to the gratification of desire, they fall downwards into a foul hell.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 16, p. 223

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam || 17 ||
translation: Self-glorifying, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform lip-sacrifices for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinance.

cross_checks.other_text: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 17, p. 223

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ || 18 ||
translation: Given over to egoism, power, insolence, lust and wrath, these malicious ones hate Me in the bodies of others and in their own.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 18, p. 223–224

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu || 19 ||
translation: These haters, evil, pitiless, vilest among men in the world, I ever throw down into demoniacal wombs.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 19, p. 224

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim || 20 ||
translation: Cast into demoniacal wombs, deluded birth after birth, attaining not to Me, O Kaunteya, they sink into the lowest depths.

cross_checks.other_text: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 20, p. 224

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

sensitivity.note: Describes "demoniacal" qualities. Use it to reflect on one's own conduct; never to label, condemn or demonize other people or groups.

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet || 21 ||
translation: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self—lust, wrath, and greed; therefore let man renounce these three.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 21, p. 224

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ।
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ |
ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim || 22 ||
translation: A man liberated from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kunti, accomplisheth his own welfare, and thus reacheth the highest goal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 22, p. 225

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः ।
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ |
na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim || 23 ||
translation: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, followeth the promptings of desire, attaineth not to perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 23, p. 225

division_title: The Yoga of Division between the Divine and the Demoniacal
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ ।
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau |
jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi || 24 ||
translation: Therefore let the Scriptures be thy authority, in determining what ought to be done, or what ought not to be done. Knowing what hath been declared by the ordinances of the Scriptures, thou oughtest to work in this world.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 16, verse 24, p. 225–226

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः ।
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayā'nvitāḥ |
teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ || 1 ||
translation: Those that sacrifice full of faith, but casting aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, what is verily their condition, O Krishna? Is it one of Purity, Passion, or Darkness?

translator_notes.text: The three qualities, Sattva, Rajah, Tamah, are here used in their moral correspondences, and are therefore translated as Purity, Passion, and Darkness

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 1, p. 227

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā |
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu || 2 ||
translation: Threefold is by nature the inborn faith of the embodied—pure, passionate, and dark. Hear thou of these.

cross_checks.other_text: त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 2, p. 227–228

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ || 3 ||
translation: The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith; that which his faith is, he is even that.

translator_notes.text: That is, the man's faith shows what is the man's character.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 3, p. 228

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
pretānbhūtagaṇāṃścānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ || 4 ||
translation: Pure men worship the Gods; the passionate the gnomes and giants; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits.

translator_notes.text: Yakshas, gnomes, are the servants of the Lord of Wealth, i. e. , are connected with metals; Râkshasas, giants, or Titans, are the gigantic inhabitants of Atlantis versed in magic and sorcery.
Pretas, ghosts, are departed men; while Bhûtas, nature-spirits, are of a somewhat goblin-like type.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 4, p. 228

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
dambhāhaṅkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ || 5 ||
translation: The men who perform severe austerities, unenjoined by the Scriptures, wedded to vanity and egoism, impelled by the force of their desires and passions,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 5, p. 229
