division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कर्शयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
karśayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ |
māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān || 6 ||
translation: Unintelligent, tormenting the aggregated elements forming the body, and Me also, seated in the inner body, know these demoniacal in their resolves.

cross_checks.other_text: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः।मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 6, p. 229

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñastapastathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu || 7 ||
translation: The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.

cross_checks.other_text: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 7, p. 229

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ || 8 ||
translation: The foods that augment vitality, energy, vigour, health, joy and cheerfulness, delicious, bland, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 8, p. 230

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कट्‌वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः ।
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ |
āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ || 9 ||
translation: The passionate desire foods that are bitter, sour, saline, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning and which produce pain, grief and sickness.

cross_checks.other_text: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 9, p. 230

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam || 10 ||
translation: That which is stale and flat, putrid and corrupt, leavings also and unclean, is the food dear to the dark.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 10, p. 230

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टोय इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭoya ijyate |
yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ || 11 ||
translation: The sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, as enjoined by the ordinances, under the firm belief that sacrifice is a duty, that is pure.

cross_checks.other_text: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 11, p. 230–231

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat |
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam || 12 ||
translation: The sacrifice offered with a view verily to fruit, and also indeed for self-glorification, O best of the Bhâratas; know thou that to be of passion.

cross_checks.other_text: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 12, p. 231

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam |
śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate || 13 ||
translation: The sacrifice contrary to the ordinances, without distributing food, devoid of words of power and without gifts, empty of faith, is said to be of darkness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 13, p. 231

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam |
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate || 14 ||
translation: Worship given to the Gods, to the twice-born, to the teachers and to the wise, purity, straightforwardness, continence and harmlessness, are called the austerity of the body.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 14, p. 231–232

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat |
svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate || 15 ||
translation: Speech causing no annoyance, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Scriptures, are called the austerity of speech.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 15, p. 232

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ |
bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate || 16 ||
translation: Mental happiness, equilibrium, silence, self-control, purity of nature—these are called the austerity of the mind.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 16, p. 232

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ |
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate || 17 ||
translation: This threefold austerity, performed by men with the utmost faith, without desire for fruit, harmonised, is said to be pure.

cross_checks.other_text: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 17, p. 232–233

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat |
kriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam || 18 ||
translation: The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining respect, honour and worship, and for ostentation, is said to be of passion, unstable and fleeting.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 18, p. 233

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 19 ||
translation: That austerity done under a deluded understanding, with self-torture, or with the object of destroying another, that is declared of darkness.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 19, p. 233

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam || 20 ||
translation: That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 20, p. 233–234

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam || 21 ||
translation: That given with a view to receiving in return, or looking for fruit again, or grudgingly, that alms is accounted of passion.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 21, p. 234

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate |
asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 22 ||
translation: That alms given at unfit place and time, and to unworthy persons, disrespectfully and contemptuously, that is declared of darkness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 22, p. 234

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ओं तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
oṃ tatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā || 23 ||
translation: "Aum Tat Sat," this has been considered to be the threefold designation of the Eternal. By that were ordained of old Brâhmanas, Vedas and sacrifices.

cross_checks.other_text: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 23, p. 234–235

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām || 24 ||
translation: Therefore with the pronunciation of "Aum" the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as laid down in the ordinances are always commenced by the knowers of the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 24, p. 235

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ |
dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ || 25 ||
translation: With the pronunciation of "Tat" and without aiming at fruit are performed the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and gift, by those desiring liberation.

cross_checks.other_text: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 25, p. 235

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate || 26 ||
translation: "Sat" is used in the sense of reality and goodness; likewise, O Pârtha, the word "Sat" is used in the sense of a good work.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 26, p. 235–236

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate |
karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate || 27 ||
translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift is also called "Sat", and action for the sake of the Supreme is also named "Sat."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 27, p. 236

division_title: The Yoga of the Division of Threefold Faith
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha || 28 ||
translation: Whatsoever is wrought without faith, oblation, gift, austerity, or other deed, "Asat" it is called, O Pârtha; it is nought, here or hereafter.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 17, verse 28, p. 236

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana || 1 ||
translation: I desire, O mighty-armed, to know severally the essence of renunciation, O Hrishîkesha, and of relinquishment, O Keshinishûdana.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 1, p. 238

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ || 2 ||
translation: Sages have known as renunciation the renouncing of works with desire; the relinquishing of the fruit of all actions is called relinquishment by the wise.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 2, p. 238

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।
यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ |
yajñadānatapaḥ karma na tyājyamiti cāpare || 3 ||
translation: "Action should be relinquished as an evil," declare some thoughtful men; "acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished," say others.

cross_checks.other_text:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः।
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 3, p. 239

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama |
tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ || 4 ||
translation: Hear my conclusions as to that relinquishment, O best of the Bhâratas; since relinquishment, O tiger of men, has been explained as threefold.

cross_checks.other_text: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 4, p. 239

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यज्ञदानतपः कर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
yajñadānatapaḥ karma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat |
yajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām || 5 ||
translation: Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the intelligent.

cross_checks.other_text: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 5, p. 239–240

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam || 6 ||
translation: But even these actions should be done leaving aside attachment and fruit, O Pârtha; that is my certain and best belief.

cross_checks.other_text: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 6, p. 240

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते ।
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate |
mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 7 ||
translation: Verily renunciation of actions that are prescribed is not proper; the relinquishment thereof from delusion is said to be of darkness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 7, p. 240

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet |
sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet || 8 ||
translation: He who relinquisheth an action from fear of physical suffering, saying "Painful," thus performing a passionate relinquishment, obtaineth not the fruit of relinquishment.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 8, p. 240

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन ।
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjuna |
saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ || 9 ||
translation: He who performeth a prescribed action, saying, "it ought to be done," O Arjuna, relinquishing attachment and also fruit, that relinquishment is regarded as pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 9, p. 241

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate |
tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ || 10 ||
translation: The relinquisher pervaded by purity, intelligent and with doubts cut away, hateth not unpleasurable action nor is attached to pleasurable.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 10, p. 241

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration:
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ |
yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate || 11 ||
translation: Nor indeed can embodied beings completely relinquish action; verily he who relinquisheth the fruit of action, he is said to be a relinquisher.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 11, p. 241

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit || 12 ||
translation: Good, evil and mixed—threefold is the fruit of action hereafter for the non-relinquisher; but there is none ever for the renouncer.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 12, p. 242

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।
साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration:
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me |
sāṅkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām || 13 ||
translation: These five causes, O mighty-armed, learn of Me as declared in the Sâñkhya system for the accomplishment of all actions:

cross_checks.other_text: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 13, p. 242

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham |
vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam || 14 ||
translation: The body, the actor, the various organs, the diverse kinds of energies, and the presiding deities also, the fifth.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 14, p. 242

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शरीरवाङ्‌मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः ।
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration:
śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ |
nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ || 15 ||
translation: Whatever action a man performeth by his body, speech and mind, whether right or the reverse, these five are the cause thereof.

cross_checks.other_text: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः।न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 15, p. 242–243

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration:
tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ |
paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ || 16 ||
translation: That being so, he verily who—owing to untrained Reason—looketh on his Self, which is isolated, as the actor, he of perverted intelligence, seeth not.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 16, p. 243

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वाऽपि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration:
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvā'pi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate || 17 ||
translation: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose Reason is not affected, though he slay these peoples, he slayeth not, nor is bound.

cross_checks.other_text: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 17, p. 243

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration:
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā |
karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṅgrahaḥ || 18 ||
translation: Knowledge, the knowable and the knower, the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action, the actor, the threefold constituents of action.

cross_checks.other_text: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 18, p. 243–244

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration:
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ |
procyate guṇasaṅkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi || 19 ||
translation: Knowledge, action and actor in the category of qualities are also said to be severally threefold, from the difference of qualities; hear thou duly these also.

cross_checks.other_text: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 19, p. 244

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration:
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate |
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam || 20 ||
translation: That by which one indestructible Being is seen in all beings, inseparate in the separated, know thou that knowledge as pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 20, p. 244

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration:
pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān |
vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam || 21 ||
translation: But that knowledge which regardeth the several manifold existences in all beings as separate, that knowledge know thou as of passion;

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 21, p. 244–245

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन् कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration:
yattu kṛtsnavadekasmin kārye saktamahaitukam |
atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 22 ||
translation: While that which clingeth to each one thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasping the reality, narrow, that is declared to be dark.

cross_checks.other_text: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम्।अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 22, p. 245

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration:
niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam |
aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate || 23 ||
translation: An action which is ordained, done by one undesirous of fruit, devoid of attachment, without love or hate, that is called pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 23, p. 245

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः ।
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration:
yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ |
kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam || 24 ||
translation: But that action that is done by one longing for desires, or again with egoism, or with much effort, that is declared to be passionate.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 24, p. 245–246

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration:
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanapekṣya ca pauruṣam |
mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate || 25 ||
translation: The action undertaken from delusion, without regard to capacity and consequences—loss and injury to others—that is declared to be dark.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 25, p. 246

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्त्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration:
muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ |
siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ karttā sāttvika ucyate || 26 ||
translation: Liberated from attachment, not egoistic, endued with firmness and confidence, unchanged by success or failure, that actor is called pure.

cross_checks.other_text: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 26, p. 246

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥ २७ ॥
transliteration:
rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ |
harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 27 ||
translation: Impassioned, desiring to obtain the fruit of actions, greedy, harmful, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an actor is pronounced passionate.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 27, p. 246

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration:
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ |
viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate || 28 ||
translation: Discordant, vulgar, stubborn, cheating, malicious, indolent, despairful, procrastinating, that actor is called dark.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 28, p. 247

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration:
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya || 29 ||
translation: The division of Reason and of firmness also, threefold according to the qualities, hear thou related, unreservedly and severally, O Dhananjaya.

cross_checks.other_text: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु।प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 29, p. 247

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration:
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 30 ||
translation: That which knoweth energy and abstinence, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, that Reason is pure, O Pârtha.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 30, p. 247

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३१ ॥
transliteration:
yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca |
ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 31 ||
translation: That by which one understandeth away Right and Wrong and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, that Reason, O Pârtha, is passionate.

translator_notes.text: Dharma and Adharma, Right and Wrong in the widest sense, law and lawlessness.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 31, p. 248

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसा वृता ।
सर्वार्थान् विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration:
adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasā vṛtā |
sarvārthān viparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 32 ||
translation: That which, enwrapped in darkness, thinketh wrong to be right and seeth all things subverted, that Reason, O Pârtha, is of darkness.

corrections.basis: English verse number misprinted or missing in the 1922 printing; numbering follows the Sanskrit text.

cross_checks.other_text: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता।सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 32, p. 248

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥ ३३ ॥
transliteration:
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ |
yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 33 ||
translation: The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, one restraineth the activity of the mind, of the life breaths and of the sense-organs, that firmness, O Pârtha, is pure.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 33, p. 248–249

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन ।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥ ३४ ॥
transliteration:
yayā tu dharmakāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna |
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 34 ||
translation: But the firmness, O Arjuna, by which, from attachment desirous of fruit, one holdeth fast duty, desire and wealth, that firmness, O Pârtha, is passionate.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 34, p. 249

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration:
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 35 ||
translation: That by which one from stupidity doth not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also vanity, that firmness, O Pârtha, is dark.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 35, p. 249

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥ ३६ ॥
transliteration:
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati || 36 ||
translation: And now the threefold kinds of pleasure hear thou from Me, O bull of the Bhâratas. That in which one by practice rejoiceth, and which putteth an end to pain;

cross_checks.other_text: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 36, p. 249–250

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥ ३७ ॥
transliteration:
yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam |
tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam || 37 ||
translation: Which at first is as venom but in the end is as nectar; that pleasure is said to be pure, born of the blissful knowledge of the Self.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 37, p. 250

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
transliteration:
viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam |
pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam || 38 ||
translation: That which from the union of the senses with their objects at first is as nectar, but in the end is like venom, that pleasure is accounted passionate.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 38, p. 250

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration:
yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ |
nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 39 ||
translation: That pleasure which both at first and afterwards is delusive of the self, arising from sleep, indolence and heedlessness, that is declared dark.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 39, p. 250–251

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥ ४० ॥
transliteration:
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ |
sattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ || 40 ||
translation: There is not an entity, either on the earth or again in heaven among the Shining Ones, that is liberated from these three qualities, born of Matter.

cross_checks.other_text: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 40, p. 251

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप ।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥ ४१ ॥
transliteration:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ || 41 ||
translation: Of Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaishyas and Shûdras, O Parantapa, the duties have been distributed, according to the qualities born of their own natures.

translator_notes.text: Karma; it is action arising from the nature fashioned by past thoughts and desires.

cross_checks.other_text: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप।कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 41, p. 251

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४२ ॥
transliteration:
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam || 42 ||
translation: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, wisdom, knowledge, belief in God, are the Brâhmana duty, born of his own nature.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 42, p. 251–252

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥ ४३ ॥
transliteration:
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam || 43 ||
translation: Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity, and also not flying from battle, generosity, the nature of a ruler, are the Kshattriya duty, born of his own nature.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 43, p. 252

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥ ४४ ॥
transliteration:
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam || 44 ||
translation: Ploughing, protection of kine, and trade are the Vaishya duty, born of his own nature. Action of the nature of service is the Shûdra duty, born of his own nature.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 44, p. 252

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥ ४५ ॥
transliteration:
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu || 45 ||
translation: Man reacheth perfection by each being intent on his own duty. Listen thou how perfection is won by him who is intent on his own duty.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 45, p. 253

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥ ४६ ॥
transliteration:
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ || 46 ||
translation: He from whom is the emanation of beings, by Whom all This is pervaded, by worshipping Him in his own duty a man winneth perfection.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 46, p. 253

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रेयान् स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४७ ॥
transliteration:
śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 47 ||
translation: Better is one's own duty though destitute of merits than the well-executed duty of another. He who doeth the duty laid down by his own nature incurreth not sin.

translator_notes.text: Dharma. There is a subtle difference in these words, here used almost interchangeably. Karma arises from the past; Dharma also so arises, but implies also the law by which the next step in evolution is made.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥ ४८ ॥
transliteration:
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ || 48 ||
translation: Congenital duty, O son of Kunti, though defective, ought not to be abandoned. All undertakings indeed are clouded by defects as fire by smoke.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 48, p. 254

sensitivity.note: Concerns varna (social classes), birth or women. Interpretations differ — for example, whether varna rests on qualities and actions (4.13) or on birth — and the 1922 translation's wording reflects its era. Never use these verses to justify discrimination by caste, birth or gender.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥ ४९ ॥
transliteration:
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati || 49 ||
translation: He whose Reason is everywhere unattached, the self-subdued, dead to desires, he goeth by renunciation to the supreme perfection of freedom from obligation.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 49, p. 254

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाऽऽप्नोति निबोध मे ।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥ ५० ॥
transliteration:
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathā''pnoti nibodha me |
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā || 50 ||
translation: How he who hath attained perfection obtaineth the Eternal, that highest state of wisdom, learn thou from Me only succinctly, O Kaunteya.

cross_checks.other_text: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 50, p. 255

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥ ५१ ॥
transliteration:
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyā''tmānaṃ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca || 51 ||
translation: United to this Reason, purified, controlling the self by firmness, having abandoned sound and the other objects of the senses, having laid aside passion and malice,

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च।शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 51, p. 255

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥ ५२ ॥
transliteration:
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ || 52 ||
translation: Dwelling in solitude, abstemious, speech, body and mind subdued, constantly fixed in meditation and yoga, taking refuge in dispassion,

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 52, p. 255

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ ५३ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate || 53 ||
translation: Having cast aside egoism, violence, arrogance, desire, wrath, covetousness, selfless and peaceful—he is fit to become the Eternal.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 53, p. 256

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥ ५४ ॥
transliteration:
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām || 54 ||
translation: Becoming the Eternal, serene in the Self, he neither grieveth nor desireth; the same to all beings, he obtaineth supreme devotion unto Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 54, p. 256

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
transliteration:
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ |
tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram || 55 ||
translation: By devotion he knoweth Me in essence, who and what I am; having thus known Me in essence he forthwith entereth into the Supreme.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 55, p. 256

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥ ५६ ॥
transliteration:
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ |
matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam || 56 ||
translation: Though ever performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, by My grace he obtaineth the eternal indestructible abode.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 56, p. 256–257

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥ ५७ ॥
transliteration:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava || 57 ||
translation: Renouncing mentally all works in Me, intent on Me, resorting to the yoga of discrimination, have thy thought ever on Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 57, p. 257

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥ ५८ ॥
transliteration:
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṅkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi || 58 ||
translation: Thinking on Me, thou shalt overcome all obstacles by My grace: but if from egoism thou wilt not listen, thou shalt be destroyed utterly.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 58, p. 257

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥ ५९ ॥
transliteration:
yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati || 59 ||
translation: Entrenched in egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight;" to no purpose thy determination; nature will constrain thee.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 59, p. 257–258

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥ ६० ॥
transliteration:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat || 60 ||
translation: O son of Kuntî, bound by thine own duty born of thine own nature, that which from delusion thou desirest not to do, even that helplessly thou shalt perform.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 60, p. 258

sensitivity.note: In context, Krishna urges Arjuna to fight in a specific war. Never use it to encourage violence, revenge or harming anyone; at most it speaks to facing a hard duty instead of avoiding it.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ ६१ ॥
transliteration:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā || 61 ||
translation: The Lord dwelleth in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, by His illusive Power causing all beings to revolve, as though mounted on a potter's wheel.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 61, p. 258

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥ ६२ ॥
transliteration:
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam || 62 ||
translation: Flee unto Him for shelter with all thy being, O Bhârata; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace, the everlasting dwelling-place.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 62, p. 258

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥ ६३ ॥
transliteration:
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru || 63 ||
translation: Thus hath wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected on it fully, then act thou as thou listest.

cross_checks.other_text: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 63, p. 259

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥ ६४ ॥
transliteration:
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam || 64 ||
translation: Listen thou again to My supreme word, most secret of all; beloved art thou of Me, and steadfast of heart, therefore will I speak for thy benefit.

cross_checks.other_text: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 64, p. 259

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥ ६५ ॥
transliteration:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me || 65 ||
translation: Merge thy mind in Me, be my devotee, sacrifice to Me, prostrate thyself before Me, thou shalt come even to Me. I pledge thee My troth; thou art dear to Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 65, p. 259

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥ ६६ ॥
transliteration:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ || 66 ||
translation: Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.

cross_checks.other_text: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 66, p. 260

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥ ६७ ॥
transliteration:
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana |
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati || 67 ||
translation: Never is this to be spoken by thee to anyone who is without asceticism, nor without devotion, nor to one who desireth not to listen, nor yet to him who speaketh evil of Me.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 67, p. 260

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥ ६८ ॥
transliteration:
ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati |
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayam || 68 ||
translation: He who shall declare this supreme secret among My devotees, having shown the highest devotion for Me, without doubt he shall come to Me.

translator_notes.text: Some read "asamsayah," which would mean "being freed from doubts."

cross_checks.other_text: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 68, p. 260

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥ ६९ ॥
transliteration:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ |
bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi || 69 ||
translation: Nor is there any among men who performeth dearer service to Me than he, nor any other shall be more beloved by Me on earth than he.

cross_checks.other_text: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः।भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 69, p. 261

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥ ७० ॥
transliteration:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ || 70 ||
translation: And he who shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of wisdom. Such is My mind.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 70, p. 261

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभांल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ ७१ ॥
transliteration:
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ |
so'pi muktaḥ śubhāṃllokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām || 71 ||
translation: The man also who, full of faith, merely heareth it unreviling, even he, freed from evil, obtaineth the radiant worlds of the righteous.

cross_checks.other_text: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः।सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 71, p. 261

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Krishna
sanskrit:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रणष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥ ७२ ॥
transliteration:
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā |
kaccidajñānasammohaḥ praṇaṣṭaste dhanañjaya || 72 ||
translation: Hath this been heard, O son of Prithâ, with one-pointed mind? Has thy delusion, caused by unwisdom, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

cross_checks.other_text: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा।कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 72, p. 261–262

provenance_notes: Sanskrit differs from the cross-check edition; shown as printed in the primary edition until reviewed.

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Arjuna
sanskrit:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाऽच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥ ७३ ॥
transliteration:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayā'cyuta |
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava || 73 ||
translation: Destroyed is my delusion. I have gained knowledge through Thy grace, O Immutable one. I am firm, my doubts have fled away. I will do according to Thy word.

corrections.basis: Marked [sic] by Wikisource transcribers. Confirmed by the cross-check edition.

cross_checks.other_text: नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत।स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 73, p. 262

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥ ७४ ॥
transliteration:
ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ |
saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam || 74 ||
translation: I heard this marvellous dialogue of Vâsudeva, and of the great-souled Partha, causing my hair to stand on end.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 74, p. 262

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद् गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥ ७५ ॥
transliteration:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetad guhyamahaṃ param |
yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam || 75 ||
translation: By the favour of Vyâsa I listened to this secret and supreme yoga from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself, speaking before mine eyes.

cross_checks.other_text: व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम्।योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 75, p. 263

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ७६ ॥
transliteration:
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam |
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ || 76 ||
translation: O King, remembering, remembering this marvellous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 76, p. 263

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥ ७७ ॥
transliteration:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ || 77 ||
translation: Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 77, p. 263

division_title: The Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation
speaker: Sanjaya
sanskrit:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥ ७८ ॥
transliteration:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama || 78 ||
translation: Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. So I think.

translator_notes.text: Shri Shankaracharya's reading would run, translated: "There is prosperity, victory, happiness, and firm morality."

citation.label: Annie Besant (tr.), The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed. (1922), Discourse 18, verse 78, p. 263–264

translation: All this, whatsoever exists in the universe, should be covered by the Lord. Having renounced (the unreal), enjoy (the Real). Do not covet the wealth of any man.

translator_notes.text: We cover all things with the Lord by perceiving the Divine Presence everywhere. When the consciousness is firmly fixed in God, the conception of diversity naturally drops away; because the One Cosmic Existence shines through all things. As we gain the light of wisdom, we cease to cling to the unrealities of this world and we find all our joy in the realm of Reality.

The word "enjoy" is also interpreted by the great commentator Sankaracharya as "protect," because knowledge of our true Self is the greatest protector and sustainer. If we do not have this knowledge, we cannot be happy; because nothing on this external plane of phenomena is permanent or dependable. He who is rich in the knowledge of the Self does not covet external power or possession.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 1

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: If one should desire to live in this world a hundred years, one should live performing Karma (righteous deeds). Thus thou mayest live; there is no other way. By doing this, Karma (the fruits of thy actions) will not defile thee.

translator_notes.text: If a man still clings to long life and earthly possessions, and is therefore unable to follow the path of Self-knowledge (Gnana-Nishta) as prescribed in the first Mantram (text), then he may follow the path of right action (Karma-Nishta). Karma here means actions performed without selfish motive, for the sake of the Lord alone. When a man performs actions clinging blindly to his lower desires, then his actions bind him to the plane of ignorance or the plane of birth and death; but when the same actions are performed with surrender to God, they purify and liberate him.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 2

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: After leaving their bodies, they who have killed the Self go to the worlds of the Asuras, covered with blinding ignorance.

translator_notes.text: The idea of rising to bright regions as a reward for well-doers, and of falling into realms of darkness as a punishment for evil-doers is common to all great religions. But Vedanta claims that this condition of heaven and hell is only temporary; because our actions, being finite, can produce only a finite result.

What does it mean "to kill the Self?" How can the immortal Soul ever be destroyed? It cannot be destroyed, it can only be obscured. Those who hold themselves under the sway of ignorance, who serve the flesh and neglect the Atman or the real Self, are not able to perceive the effulgent and indestructible nature of their Soul; hence they fall into the realm where the Soul light does not shine. Here the Upanishad shows that the only hell is absence of knowledge. As long as man is overpowered by the darkness of ignorance, he is the slave of Nature and must accept whatever comes as the fruit of his thoughts and deeds. When he strays into the path of unreality, the Sages declare that he destroys himself; because he who clings to the perishable body and regards it as his true Self must experience death many times.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 3

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: That One, though motionless, is swifter than the mind. The senses can never overtake It, for It ever goes before. Though immovable, It travels faster than those who run. By It the all-pervading air sustains all living beings.

translator_notes.text: This verse explains the character of the Atman or Self. A finite object can be taken from one place and put in another, but it can only occupy one space at a time. The Atman, however, is present everywhere; hence, though one may run with the greatest swiftness to overtake It, already It is there before him.
Even the all-pervading air must be supported by this Self, since It is infinite; and as nothing can live without breathing air, all living things must draw their life from the Cosmic Self.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 4

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: It moves and It moves not. It is far and also It is near. It is within and also It is without all this.

translator_notes.text: It is near to those who have the power to understand It, for It dwells in the heart of every one; but It seems far to those whose mind is covered by the clouds of sensuality and self-delusion. It is within, because It is the innermost Soul of all creatures; and It is without as the essence of the whole external universe, infilling it like the all-pervading ether.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 5

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: He who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings, he never turns away from It (the Self).

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 6

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: He who perceives all beings as the Self for him how can there be delusion or grief, when he sees this oneness (everywhere)?

translator_notes.text: He who perceives the Self everywhere never shrinks from anything, because through his higher consciousness he feels united with all life. When a man sees God in all beings and all beings in God, and also God dwelling in his own Soul, how can he hate any living thing? Grief and delusion rest upon a belief in diversity, which leads to competition and all forms of selfishness. With the realization of oneness, the sense of diversity vanishes and the cause of misery is removed.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 7

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: He (the Self) is all-encircling, resplendent, bodiless, spotless, without sinews, pure, untouched by sin, all-seeing, all-knowing, transcendent, self-existent; He has disposed all things duly for eternal years.

translator_notes.text: This text defines the real nature of the Self. When our mind is cleansed from the dross of matter, then alone can we behold the vast, radiant, subtle, ever-pure and spotless Self, the true basis of our existence.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 8

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: They enter into blind darkness who worship Avidya (ignorance and delusion); they fall, as it were, into greater darkness who worship Vidya (knowledge).

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 9

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: By Vidya one end is attained; by Avidya, another. Thus we have heard from the wise men who taught this.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 10

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: He who knows at the same time both Vidya and Avidya, crosses over death by Avidya and attains immortality through Vidya.

translator_notes.text: Those who follow or "worship" the path of selfishness and pleasure (Avidya), without knowing anything higher, necessarily fall into darkness; but those who worship or cherish Vidya (knowledge) for mere intellectual pride and satisfaction, fall into greater darkness, because the opportunity which they misuse is greater.

In the subsequent verses Vidya and Avidya are used in something the same sense as "faith" and "works" in the Christian Bible; neither alone can lead to the ultimate goal, but when taken together they carry one to the Highest. Work done with unselfish motive purifies the mind and enables man to perceive his undying nature. From this he gains inevitably a knowledge of God, because the Soul and God are one and inseparable; and when he knows himself to be one with the Supreme and Indestructible Whole, he realizes his immortality.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 11

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: They fall into blind darkness who worship the Unmanifested and they fall into greater darkness who worship the manifested.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 12

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: By the worship of the Unmanifested one end is attained; by the worship of the manifested, another. Thus we have heard from the wise men who taught us this.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 13

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: He who knows at the same time both the Unmanifested (the cause of manifestation) and the destructible or manifested, he crosses over death through knowledge of the destructible and attains immortality through knowledge of the First Cause (Unmanifested).

translator_notes.text: This particular Upanishad deals chiefly with the Invisible Cause and the visible manifestation, and the whole trend of its teaching is to show that they are one and the same, one being the outcome of the other hence no perfect knowledge is possible without simultaneous comprehension of both. The wise men declare that he who worships in a one-sided way, whether the visible or the invisible, does not reach the highest goal. Only he who has a co-ordinated understanding of both the visible and the invisible, of matter and spirit, of activity and that which is behind activity, conquers Nature and thus overcomes death. By work, by making the mind steady and by following the prescribed rules given in the Scriptures, a man gains wisdom. By the light of that wisdom he is able to perceive the Invisible Cause in all visible forms. Therefore the wise man sees Him in every manifested form. They who have a true conception of God are never separated from Him. They exist in Him and He in them.

translation: O Pushan! O Sun, sole traveller of the heavens, controller of all, son of Prajapati, withdraw Thy rays and gather up Thy burning effulgence. Now through Thy Grace I behold Thy blessed and glorious form. The Purusha (Effulgent Being) who dwells within Thee, I am He.

translator_notes.text: Here the sun, who is the giver of all light, is used as the symbol of the Infinite, giver of all wisdom. The seeker after Truth prays to the Effulgent One to control His dazzling rays, that his eyes, no longer blinded by them, may behold the Truth. Having perceived It, he proclaims: "Now I see that that Effulgent Being and I are one and the same, and my delusion is destroyed." By the light of Truth he is able to discriminate between the real and the unreal, and the knowledge thus gained convinces him that he is one with the Supreme; that there is no difference between himself and the Supreme Truth; or as Christ said, "I and my Father are one."

translation: May my life-breath go to the all-pervading and immortal Prana, and let this body be burned to ashes. Om! O mind, remember thy deeds! O mind, remember, remember thy deeds! Remember!

translator_notes.text: Seek not fleeting results as the reward of thy actions, O mind! Strive only for the Imperishable. This Mantram or text is often chanted at the hour of death to remind one of the perishable nature of the body and the eternal nature of the Soul. When the clear vision of the distinction between the mortal body and the immortal Soul dawns in the heart, then all craving for physical pleasure or material possession drops away; and one can say, let the body be burned to ashes that the Soul may attain its freedom; for death is nothing more than the casting-off of a worn-out garment.

citation.label: Swami Paramananda (tr.), The Upanishads (1919), Isha Upanishad, verse 17

provenance_notes: English translation only: this edition does not print the Sanskrit, and no second edition has been compared yet.

translation: O Agni (Bright Being)! Lead us to blessedness by the good path. O Lord! Thou knowest all our deeds, remove all evil and delusion from us. To Thee we offer our prostrations and supplications again and again.

translator_notes.text: This Upanishad is called Isa-Vasya-Upanishad, that which gives Brahma-Vidya or knowledge of the All-pervading Deity. The dominant thought running through it is that we cannot enjoy life or realize true happiness unless we consciously "cover" all with the Omnipresent Lord. If we are not fully conscious of that which sustains our life, how can we live wisely and perform our duties? Whatever we see, movable or immovable, good or bad, it is all "That." We must not divide our conception of the universe; for in dividing it, we have only fragmentary knowledge and we thus limit ourselves.

He who sees all beings in his Self and his Self in all beings, he never suffers; because when he sees all creatures within his true Self, then jealousy, grief and hatred vanish. He alone can love. That AH-pervading One is self- effulgent, birthless, deathless, pure, untainted by sin and sorrow. Knowing this, he becomes free from the bondage of matter and transcends death. Transcending death means realizing the difference between body and Soul and identifying oneself with the Soul. When we actually behold the undecaying Soul within us and realize our true nature, we no longer identify ourself with the body which dies and we do not die with the body.

Self-knowledge has always been the theme of the Sages; and the Upanishads deal especially with the knowledge of the Self and also with the knowledge of God, because there is no difference between the Self and God. They are one and the same. That which comes out of the Infinite Whole must also be infinite; hence the Self is infinite. That is the ocean, we are the drops. So long as the drop remains separate from the ocean, it is small and weak; but when it is one with the ocean, then it has all the strength of the ocean. Similarly, so long as man believes himself to be separate from the Whole, he is helpless; but when he identifies himself with It, then he transcends all weakness and partakes of Its omnipotent qualities.
